# Plan 15: Survivor Vocations, Personal Arcs, and Shelter Culture

**Status:** Starter expansion wave plus Continuation Wave 2; documentation-only, premise-gated, and not an implementation claim. **Wave target:** Plans 13–16 synchronized multi-edit, with distinct mechanics, story content, locations, shelter lore, character arcs, factions, and late-game material.

**Domain:** survivor vocations, personal story arcs, shelter culture, mentorship, and everyday belonging.

**Current-owner boundary:** Candidate work must route through survivor roster, RelationshipDecaySystem and existing relationship owner, skill progression, duty and needs systems, HobbySystem, SurvivorEducationSystem, ShelterArchiveSystem, and current journal routing. No second faction ledger, relationship store, map graph, shelter counter, ending resolver, legacy store, or parallel save section may be created.

## Scope and non-duplication contract

This plan treats a name card with a red stitch, a vocation badge, a shared meal bowl, and a shelter mural under dust as authored anchors for a new playable layer. They are not assumed to exist in the shipped catalog. The current source audit must verify IDs, consumers, host construction, save registration, and live claims before any row becomes implementation-ready. The proposed signals — confidence, affinity, fatigue, vocation fit, room belonging, mentorship continuity, and arc readiness — are read models or content prerequisites until an owner is named.

The proposed cast and political vocabulary are deliberately provisional: the Hearth Circle, Ledgerhands, Dust Choir, Lantern Apprentices, and the proposed late-game Common Table. The late-game proposal is a proposed late-game Common Table faction that represents a shelter culture coalition, with no new standing owner and no replacement for existing relationships, education, hobby, or archive systems. Existing diplomacy, standing, relationship, map, roster, archive, campaign, ending, and legacy behavior remains authoritative. Where an existing system already expresses a requested outcome, this plan supplies content, projection, UX, or a bridge rather than a replacement.

## Nine synchronized expansion passes

### Pass 1: Name Card Census

#### Field 1 — Canon, premise, and evidence boundary

This pass turns the proposal into a reviewable slice with a named owner and a visible player outcome. Start from the roster and relationship census. The plan adds authored vocation labels, personal arc triggers, and shelter culture projections only where existing survivor, skill, relationship, hobby, education, and archive owners provide a seam. A vocation is a playable lens on current work and learning, not a second class system with hidden bonuses. In this pass, the mentor is the concrete review token: it must be visible in data, UI, journal, or a focused assertion before the slice can advance. The design review should name the owning file or public seam, the source fact that proves the premise, and the smallest observable result a player would see. If the source or catalog differs, record the divergence and stop at the boundary instead of inventing a compensating authority. That discipline keeps this field useful for a builder, a writer, a UI implementer, and a reviewer working from the same contract.

#### Field 2 — Player loop and moment-to-moment decisions

This pass turns the proposal into a reviewable slice with a named owner and a visible player outcome. Make the loop intimate and legible: assign a duty, notice a friction, invite a mentor, schedule a shared activity, respond to a setback, and record what changed. The player should see why a survivor accepts or refuses a role. Existing needs, fatigue, morale, and relationship values remain authoritative; this plan supplies content, timing, and presentation around them. In this pass, the memory is the concrete review token: it must be visible in data, UI, journal, or a focused assertion before the slice can advance. The design review should name the owning file or public seam, the source fact that proves the premise, and the smallest observable result a player would see. If the source or catalog differs, record the divergence and stop at the boundary instead of inventing a compensating authority. That discipline keeps this field useful for a builder, a writer, a UI implementer, and a reviewer working from the same contract.

#### Field 3 — New mechanic and systemic rules

This pass turns the proposal into a reviewable slice with a named owner and a visible player outcome. A vocation can unlock a set of authored actions such as “teach a safer knot,” “repair a stove grate,” “name a new child,” or “host the late meal.” Outcomes may grant existing skill progress, morale, journal entries, or archive records. They should never write directly to multiple systems without a host command that defines ordering, idempotency, and failure behavior. In this pass, the mural is the concrete review token: it must be visible in data, UI, journal, or a focused assertion before the slice can advance. The design review should name the owning file or public seam, the source fact that proves the premise, and the smallest observable result a player would see. If the source or catalog differs, record the divergence and stop at the boundary instead of inventing a compensating authority. That discipline keeps this field useful for a builder, a writer, a UI implementer, and a reviewer working from the same contract.

#### Field 4 — Locations, shelter spaces, and environmental lore

This pass turns the proposal into a reviewable slice with a named owner and a visible player outcome. Shelter lore lives in spaces. The Common Room preserves a bowl with three repaired cracks; the repair alcove smells of graphite; the old classroom keeps chalk on a nail; the meal line is where news travels fastest; the memorial wall is polished by hand; the north gallery holds blankets folded according to absent people. Each room reference must map to a live facility or remain explicitly content-only. In this pass, the room is the concrete review token: it must be visible in data, UI, journal, or a focused assertion before the slice can advance. The design review should name the owning file or public seam, the source fact that proves the premise, and the smallest observable result a player would see. If the source or catalog differs, record the divergence and stop at the boundary instead of inventing a compensating authority. That discipline keeps this field useful for a builder, a writer, a UI implementer, and a reviewer working from the same contract.

#### Field 5 — Character personalities, factions, and late-game cast

This pass turns the proposal into a reviewable slice with a named owner and a visible player outcome. Write personalities through choices and rhythms. Mara explains a repair twice without shaming anyone, Joren judges a recipe by whether children can eat it, Nell turns every question into a lesson, Ivo jokes when afraid, and Tavi paints over old warning signs only after asking who remembers them. Their arc state reads current relationship and roster facts, with authored flags scoped to the scene or quest. In this pass, the memory is the concrete review token: it must be visible in data, UI, journal, or a focused assertion before the slice can advance. The design review should name the owning file or public seam, the source fact that proves the premise, and the smallest observable result a player would see. #### Field 6 — Authored data, content schema, and catalog validation

This pass turns the proposal into a reviewable slice with a named owner and a visible player outcome. Data candidates should include vocation definitions, mentor invitations, scene beats, dialogue variants, cultural rituals, and arc rewards. Each row needs schema_version, owner, stable ID, required current IDs, content tags, effect route, fallback text, and archive policy. If the source or catalog differs, record the divergence and stop at the boundary instead of inventing a compensating authority. That discipline keeps this field useful for a builder, a writer, a UI implementer, and a reviewer working from the same contract.

#### Field 7 — Persistence, deterministic replay, and migration seams

This pass turns the proposal into a reviewable slice with a named owner and a visible player outcome. Personal arcs need durable but small state. Capture active arc ID, completed beat IDs, mentor pair, last offered day, and unresolved consent prompt through an existing journal or campaign save seam selected after premise review. Any seeded social variation uses campaign seed plus arc and beat IDs. Restores must not replay a meal, reward, or memorial line twice. The design review should name the owning file or public seam, the source fact that proves the premise, and the smallest observable result a player would see. #### Field 8 — Host routing, UI scaffolding, UX, accessibility, and performance

This pass turns the proposal into a reviewable slice with a named owner and a visible player outcome. The UI should show a vocation card, a mentor fit explanation, and a shelter culture timeline without turning private feelings into a spreadsheet. Provide readable tooltips, text alternatives for mural colors, focus order across roster and action controls, and predictable back behavior. #### Field 9 — Storylines, prose, side quests, and consequence writing

This pass turns the proposal into a reviewable slice with a named owner and a visible player outcome. Side quests should move between quiet prose and practical choice: ask Mara to teach a rival, help Joren feed a guest faction, let Nell choose a student, follow Ivo into an unsafe shortcut, or decide whether Tavi paints a name before the memorial is complete. The player can value efficiency, dignity, tradition, or openness, and each choice should leave a specific archive or relationship fact. In this pass, the mentor is the concrete review token: it must be visible in data, UI, journal, or a focused assertion before the slice can advance. The design review should name the owning file or public seam, the source fact that proves the premise, and the smallest observable result a player would see. If the source or catalog differs, record the divergence and stop at the boundary instead of inventing a compensating authority. That discipline keeps this field useful for a builder, a writer, a UI implementer, and a reviewer working from the same contract.

#### Field 10 — Verification, rollout order, rollback, and handoff

This pass turns the proposal into a reviewable slice with a named owner and a visible player outcome. The first safe slice is one survivor pair, one vocation lens, one mentor invitation, one shared activity, and one archive entry. Verify current roster APIs, relationship decay semantics, hobby and education ownership, needs costs, and save capture. Rollback means removing unclaimed scene rows and restoring no gameplay counters because the plan must not own a mutable parallel store. In this pass, the meal is the concrete review token: it must be visible in data, UI, journal, or a focused assertion before the slice can advance. The design review should name the owning file or public seam, the source fact that proves the premise, and the smallest observable result a player would see. **Pass 1 receipt:** The Name Card Census pass is complete as a planning artifact when its ten fields have current evidence, one owner each, a bounded first slice, and an explicit unresolved question list. No production change is implied.

Every line has a speaker or surface, localization key, tone note, and fallback behavior. Start from the roster and relationship census. The plan adds authored vocation labels, personal arc triggers, and shelter culture projections only where existing survivor, skill, relationship, hobby, education, and archive owners provide a seam. A vocation is a playable lens on current work and learning, not a second class system with hidden bonuses. Data candidates should include vocation definitions, mentor invitations, scene beats, dialogue variants, cultural rituals, and arc rewards. Each row needs schema_version, owner, stable ID, required current IDs, content tags, effect route, fallback text, and archive policy. Catalog validation must reject duplicate survivor IDs, dangling facility references, and implicit skill grants.

## Twelve story and side-quest packets

### Story packet 1: The Red Stitch

Mara marks a name card with red thread after a failed repair lesson. The player can hide the mark, explain it, or let the survivor choose its meaning. The packet must state its start condition, player choice, existing authority it calls, failure state, archive fact, and a short alternate line for a player who arrives late. The prose is a playable surface, not a substitute for the mechanic, data contract, save behavior, or UI route.

### Story packet 2: Joren's Late Meal

Joren saves a bowl for someone who never returns. Serving it to a hungry child, preserving it for a memorial, or sharing it with a guest each tells the shelter what care means. The packet must state its start condition, player choice, existing authority it calls, failure state, archive fact, and a short alternate line for a player who arrives late. The prose is a playable surface, not a substitute for the mechanic, data contract, save behavior, or UI route.

### Story packet 3: Nell's Question

Nell asks a student to teach back a lesson. A wrong answer opens a patient side quest instead of a punishment route. The packet must state its start condition, player choice, existing authority it calls, failure state, archive fact, and a short alternate line for a player who arrives late. The prose is a playable surface, not a substitute for the mechanic, data contract, save behavior, or UI route.

### Story packet 4: Ivo's Shortcut

Ivo knows a faster way through the shelter but it crosses a room that still belongs to grief. The player chooses efficiency, permission, or a new route. The packet must state its start condition, player choice, existing authority it calls, failure state, archive fact, and a short alternate line for a player who arrives late. The prose is a playable surface, not a substitute for the mechanic, data contract, save behavior, or UI route.

### Story packet 5: Tavi's Wall

Tavi paints a mural over an old warning and leaves one corner visible. The shelter must decide whether memory requires a clean wall. The packet must state its start condition, player choice, existing authority it calls, failure state, archive fact, and a short alternate line for a player who arrives late. The prose is a playable surface, not a substitute for the mechanic, data contract, save behavior, or UI route.

### Story packet 6: The Common Room Bowl

The cracked bowl moves from hand to hand during a shared activity. Its history becomes a small archive entry that outlives the immediate bonus. The packet must state its start condition, player choice, existing authority it calls, failure state, archive fact, and a short alternate line for a player who arrives late. The prose is a playable surface, not a substitute for the mechanic, data contract, save behavior, or UI route.

### Story packet 7: Apprentice Refusal

A student refuses the vocation badge because the last holder died. The player can offer another path, preserve the badge, or ask the student to name a new symbol. The packet must state its start condition, player choice, existing authority it calls, failure state, archive fact, and a short alternate line for a player who arrives late. The prose is a playable surface, not a substitute for the mechanic, data contract, save behavior, or UI route.

### Story packet 8: The Empty Bed

Room belonging is tested when an old bed is reassigned. The scene should acknowledge absence without making grief a simple morale penalty. The packet must state its start condition, player choice, existing authority it calls, failure state, archive fact, and a short alternate line for a player who arrives late. The prose is a playable surface, not a substitute for the mechanic, data contract, save behavior, or UI route.

### Story packet 9: Hearth Circle Meeting

The culture faction begins with a disagreement over who cooks, teaches, and speaks. A practical rota becomes the first political document of the Common Table. The packet must state its start condition, player choice, existing authority it calls, failure state, archive fact, and a short alternate line for a player who arrives late. The prose is a playable surface, not a substitute for the mechanic, data contract, save behavior, or UI route.

### Story packet 10: The Mentor Thread

Two survivors share a repair method but not a worldview. A mentor scene can end in consent, distance, or a new form of collaboration. The packet must state its start condition, player choice, existing authority it calls, failure state, archive fact, and a short alternate line for a player who arrives late. The prose is a playable surface, not a substitute for the mechanic, data contract, save behavior, or UI route.

### Story packet 11: Memorial Lesson

Nell turns a memorial into a lesson only after asking permission. The player can make the archive public, private, or deliberately unfinished. The packet must state its start condition, player choice, existing authority it calls, failure state, archive fact, and a short alternate line for a player who arrives late. The prose is a playable surface, not a substitute for the mechanic, data contract, save behavior, or UI route.

### Story packet 12: Common Table

The late coalition offers no throne. It offers a table plan, a shared rule for welcome, and a blank name card for whoever arrives next. The packet must state its start condition, player choice, existing authority it calls, failure state, archive fact, and a short alternate line for a player who arrives late. ## Ten systemic integration bridges

### Campaign bridge

Route the feature through current campaign state and existing quest flags. The bridge consumes confidence, affinity, fatigue, vocation fit, room belonging, mentorship continuity, and arc readiness as derived evidence and emits one named fact for campaign routing; it does not add a second campaign clock. The acceptance artifact is a source reference, an input/output example, and a focused check that proves the bridge is single-owner and observable.

### Faction bridge

Route standing or faction consequences through the canonical faction authority. Candidate groups such as the Hearth Circle, Ledgerhands, Dust Choir, Lantern Apprentices, and the proposed late-game Common Table remain provisional until IDs, aliases, and sinks are verified. The acceptance artifact is a source reference, an input/output example, and a focused check that proves the bridge is single-owner and observable.

### Relationship bridge

Read relationship and trust through the current survivor owner. A scene flag can remember a beat, but pair affinity, decay, grief, and consent remain with the existing system. The acceptance artifact is a source reference, an input/output example, and a focused check that proves the bridge is single-owner and observable.

### Exploration bridge

Use current map, expedition, vehicle, and route seams for the Common Room, the repair alcove, the old classroom, the meal line, the memorial wall, and the north sleeping gallery. New route or location content must project onto existing discovery and travel state. The acceptance artifact is a source reference, an input/output example, and a focused check that proves the bridge is single-owner and observable.

### Shelter bridge

Use current facilities, expansion, power, water, needs, and archive consumers. A lore packet may describe a room, but it cannot create a duplicate room capacity or resource balance. The acceptance artifact is a source reference, an input/output example, and a focused check that proves the bridge is single-owner and observable.

### Data bridge

Add only schema-valid, snake_case candidate data with explicit references and migration notes. Validate IDs, ranges, localization keys, and consumer reachability before writing more volume. The acceptance artifact is a source reference, an input/output example, and a focused check that proves the bridge is single-owner and observable.

### Save bridge

Capture only non-recomputable authored progress and processed IDs in the selected owner. Require round-trip and legacy fixture evidence before calling a slice persistent. The acceptance artifact is a source reference, an input/output example, and a focused check that proves the bridge is single-owner and observable.

### Determinism bridge

Use seeded keyed inputs with stable ordering. Paired replay should match outcomes, archive IDs, event order, and epilogue selection across save/load. The acceptance artifact is a source reference, an input/output example, and a focused check that proves the bridge is single-owner and observable.

### UI bridge

Expose existing commands with truthful state, focus-safe navigation, readable copy, and disposal. Panels, radio, journal, and archive views remain adapters over facts. The acceptance artifact is a source reference, an input/output example, and a focused check that proves the bridge is single-owner and observable.

### Performance bridge

Bound catalog loading, archive queries, route previews, and long prose. Prefer indexed projections and batched records; document a budget and a rollback path if the slice exceeds it. The acceptance artifact is a source reference, an input/output example, and a focused check that proves the bridge is single-owner and observable.

## First safe implementation packet

1. Re-run the premise census for survivor roster, RelationshipDecaySystem and existing relationship owner, skill progression, duty and needs systems, HobbySystem, SurvivorEducationSystem, ShelterArchiveSystem, and current journal routing and attach current file paths, APIs, data IDs, save sections, host constructors, and claims from the live ledger.
2. Select one small vertical slice built from the anchors a name card with a red stitch, a vocation badge, a shared meal bowl, and a shelter mural under dust; include one player command, one canonical mutation or read projection, one visible result, one archive/journal fact, and one reload assertion.
3. Add candidate content only after schema and localization review. Keep the proposed names the Hearth Circle, Ledgerhands, Dust Choir, Lantern Apprentices, and the proposed late-game Common Table and the Common Room, the repair alcove, the old classroom, the meal line, the memorial wall, and the north sleeping gallery tagged as provisional until catalogs confirm them.
4. Run focused static and contract checks, then a deterministic paired replay if the slice consumes seeded variation. No full suite is requested by this planning wave.
5. Hand off the exact files, owner seam, evidence, limits, and rollback instructions. A plan completion receipt is not a production integration receipt.

## Acceptance and stop lines

Acceptance requires: current premise evidence; one authoritative mutation owner; candidate data that passes schema and reference review; explicit save and deterministic behavior where state exists; a reachable host route or a clearly labeled content-only row; accessible UI copy; bounded performance; and a handoff note. Stop immediately if the proposed major factions or systems duplicate an existing faction, ending, legacy, map, relationship, archive, or campaign authority, or if ownership is unclear. Report the blocker rather than improvising a parallel system.

## Documentation receipt

The starter wave and Continuation Wave 2 now provide a ten-field scaffold, twenty synchronized passes, high-volume content banks, twenty-four story packets, twenty bridge notes, and bounded first-safe-slice handoffs. They do not modify Core, Godot scenes, production JSON, tests, or the live integration ledger.

Project Common Room, repair alcove, old classroom, meal line, memorial wall, and north sleeping gallery onto current cartography, expedition, vehicle, weather, and route seams. A route proposal is not a new world graph. The evidence packet includes one source path, one data row or content key, one input/output example, and one stop condition.

### Shelter bridge

Use current facilities, expansion, power, water, needs, duty, archive, and memorial owners. Lore cannot invent a second room capacity or resource balance. The evidence packet includes one source path, one data row or content key, one input/output example, and one stop condition.

### Content bridge

Keep IDs, schema versions, localization keys, references, and consumer reachability explicit. Reject rows that cannot be reached or safely retired. The evidence packet includes one source path, one data row or content key, one input/output example, and one stop condition.

### Save bridge

Persist only non-recomputable authored progress and processed IDs in the selected existing owner. Prove round trip before adding volume. The evidence packet includes one source path, one data row or content key, one input/output example, and one stop condition.

### Determinism bridge

Use keyed seeded inputs and stable ordering. Replay must agree on consequences, records, and prose selection across reload. The evidence packet includes one source path, one data row or content key, one input/output example, and one stop condition.

### Presentation bridge

Expose truthful state with keyboard/controller focus, text equivalents, lifecycle disposal, and readable long-text behavior. The evidence packet includes one source path, one data row or content key, one input/output example, and one stop condition.

### Release bridge

Package the slice as a bounded handoff with premise evidence, focused checks, performance notes, rollback, and explicit unresolved decisions. The evidence packet includes one source path, one data row or content key, one input/output example, and one stop condition.

Persist only non-recomputable progress and processed events in an existing save owner. Specify capture, restore, migration, duplicate-event, and rollback behavior. Replays must agree on event order, record IDs, outcomes, and prose keys. The review names the smallest observable player result and the exact evidence that would prove it. If the source differs, keep the entry as a tagged proposal and stop at the boundary instead of compensating with a parallel authority. This keeps the design useful to writers, systems designers, UI implementers, and reviewers.

#### Host/UI/UX and performance

This pass closes one loop and leaves a truthful question open. The player must find the promise, understand its state, navigate it with keyboard/controller, and receive a safe fallback if data is absent or the query is large. Expose truthful state and existing commands with focus-safe navigation, controller support, text equivalents, contrast, long-text behavior, disposal, and a bounded query/load budget. Panels are adapters, not gameplay authorities. The review names the smallest observable player result and the exact evidence that would prove it. If the source differs, keep the entry as a tagged proposal and stop at the boundary instead of compensating with a parallel authority. This keeps the design useful to writers, systems designers, UI implementers, and reviewers.

#### Storyline and side-quest consequences

This pass closes one loop and leaves a truthful question open. Stage a short scene around the badge, with a quiet prose beat, a practical choice, and a consequence routed through an existing owner. Every scene has an entry condition, choice, failure or refusal, concrete consequence, archive/journal fact, and late-arrival line. Keep prose restrained and sensory, with the mechanic and data contract carrying systemic meaning. The review names the smallest observable player result and the exact evidence that would prove it. If the source differs, keep the entry as a tagged proposal and stop at the boundary instead of compensating with a parallel authority. This keeps the design useful to writers, systems designers, UI implementers, and reviewers.

#### Verification and implementation handoff

This pass closes one loop and leaves a truthful question open. The acceptance packet must include a source path, an example involving the lesson, an unresolved question, and a rollback boundary. Require premise evidence, focused data or contract checks, runtime smoke only when needed, save round trip, deterministic replay where applicable, performance notes, and rollback. A complete document is not an implementation receipt. The review names the smallest observable player result and the exact evidence that would prove it. If the source differs, keep the entry as a tagged proposal and stop at the boundary instead of compensating with a parallel authority. This keeps the design useful to writers, systems designers, UI implementers, and reviewers.

**Pass 31 receipt:** Shelter Commons Preview is planning-complete when all ten fields have evidence, owner, player result, failure behavior, and open questions.

## Twelve new story and side-quest packets

### Story packet 25: The Family Story Exchange

A survivor brings a family recipe and refuses to explain its origin. The player can accept the gift without the story or ask what may be remembered. The packet needs entry condition, player choice, owner call, refusal or failure, archive fact, and late-arrival variant. Prose is a playable surface; it does not replace the mechanic, data contract, save behavior, or UI route.

### Story packet 26: The Long Ramp

A new route through the shelter is slower but usable by everyone. The player must choose whether access is a priority or an optional improvement. The packet needs entry condition, player choice, owner call, refusal or failure, archive fact, and late-arrival variant. Prose is a playable surface; it does not replace the mechanic, data contract, save behavior, or UI route.

### Story packet 27: The Duty Swap

Two survivors trade duties and discover that both had been protecting the same secret. The player can keep the swap private, archive it, or intervene. The packet needs entry condition, player choice, owner call, refusal or failure, archive fact, and late-arrival variant. Prose is a playable surface; it does not replace the mechanic, data contract, save behavior, or UI route.

### Story packet 28: Words for Weather

Children invent a word for the dust-light. Adults debate whether it belongs in the archive. The player decides who owns a new word. The packet needs entry condition, player choice, owner call, refusal or failure, archive fact, and late-arrival variant. Prose is a playable surface; it does not replace the mechanic, data contract, save behavior, or UI route.

### Story packet 29: The Mentor Door

A mentor closes the door after a hard lesson. The player can knock, wait, or choose another teacher and leave the boundary respected. The packet needs entry condition, player choice, owner call, refusal or failure, archive fact, and late-arrival variant. Prose is a playable surface; it does not replace the mechanic, data contract, save behavior, or UI route.

### Story packet 30: Festival Memory

A small festival repeats an old song with one line omitted. The player can restore it, ask why it was removed, or write a new ending. The packet needs entry condition, player choice, owner call, refusal or failure, archive fact, and late-arrival variant. Prose is a playable surface; it does not replace the mechanic, data contract, save behavior, or UI route.

### Story packet 31: Repair Practice

A conflict is repaired with a shared task rather than an apology. The player decides whether the work counts as reconciliation. The packet needs entry condition, player choice, owner call, refusal or failure, archive fact, and late-arrival variant. Prose is a playable surface; it does not replace the mechanic, data contract, save behavior, or UI route.

### Story packet 32: Care and Craft

A craft project is useful to the medical room but belongs emotionally to its maker. The player negotiates use, credit, and consent. The packet needs entry condition, player choice, owner call, refusal or failure, archive fact, and late-arrival variant. Prose is a playable surface; it does not replace the mechanic, data contract, save behavior, or UI route.

### Story packet 33: The Young Badge

A child chooses a vocation badge that adults consider impractical. The player can support the choice, test it, or let the child decline the badge. The packet needs entry condition, player choice, owner call, refusal or failure, archive fact, and late-arrival variant. Prose is a playable surface; it does not replace the mechanic, data contract, save behavior, or UI route.

### Story packet 34: Culture Drift

The shelter notices that a custom has changed without a vote. The player can preserve the old form, name the new one, or leave the change unowned. The packet needs entry condition, player choice, owner call, refusal or failure, archive fact, and late-arrival variant. Prose is a playable surface; it does not replace the mechanic, data contract, save behavior, or UI route.

### Story packet 35: Shelter Commons Draft

The proposed Commons charter leaves one kind of work unnamed. The player adds it, rejects the charter, or asks the workers to write the clause. The packet needs entry condition, player choice, owner call, refusal or failure, archive fact, and late-arrival variant. Prose is a playable surface; it does not replace the mechanic, data contract, save behavior, or UI route.

### Story packet 36: Mural With Two Names

A mural gains two names for one person. The final scene treats identity as a living record rather than a correction task. The packet needs entry condition, player choice, owner call, refusal or failure, archive fact, and late-arrival variant. Prose is a playable surface; it does not replace the mechanic, data contract, save behavior, or UI route.

## Ten Wave 3 integration bridges

### Campaign bridge

Read current campaign flags and emit one named content fact; never add a second clock or victory state. The evidence packet must include a source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Faction bridge

Route consequences for Hearth Circle, Ledgerhands, Dust Choir, Lantern Apprentices, Common Table, and the proposed Shelter Commons through the canonical standing or diplomacy authority after ID and alias review. The evidence packet must include a source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Relationship bridge

Read trust, affinity, grief, consent, and decay from existing survivor owners; a scene beat is not a relationship ledger. The evidence packet must include a source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Map/route bridge

Project Common Room, repair alcove, old classroom, meal line, memorial wall, north sleeping gallery onto current cartography, expedition, weather, vehicle, colony, and route seams rather than creating a parallel graph. The evidence packet must include a source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Shelter bridge

Use current facility, expansion, water, power, needs, duty, archive, celebration, and memorial owners. The evidence packet must include a source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Content bridge

Validate schema, IDs, localization keys, references, reachability, and retirement before adding volume. The evidence packet must include a source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Save bridge

Capture only non-recomputable progress or processed IDs in an existing owner and prove round trip. The evidence packet must include a source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Determinism bridge

Use keyed seeded inputs and stable ordering; paired replay must match outcomes and records after reload. The evidence packet must include a source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### UI bridge

Expose truthful state with focus, controller, text equivalents, disposal, and bounded loading; panels stay adapters. The evidence packet must include a source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Handoff bridge

Attach source paths, data examples, focused checks, performance notes, rollback, and unresolved decisions. The evidence packet must include a source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

## Wave 3 deepening volume — ten high-density packets for Survivor Vocations, Personal Arcs, and Shelter Culture

These packets increase authoring volume without adding new top-level fields. ### Deepening packet 1: family story cards

Family story cards is treated as a compact content and systems packet. Start with a current-source census: locate the owner, public API, catalog row, event producer, save section, host binding, and any existing plan claim. Define the player-facing loop in six beats: prepare, inspect, choose, commit, receive feedback, and decide what to do next. Give the packet one named mechanic, one location or shelter image, one character or faction voice, one failure state, and one late-game callback. Every packet is a proposal until its current owner, catalog reference, consumer, save seam, and host route are proven. It should state what the player sees, what can fail, and which existing fact is authoritative. It may enrich a journal, archive, radio, or epilogue surface, but it may not create a parallel ledger or a hidden authority. Candidate data uses schema_version, stable snake_case IDs, explicit references, localization keys, fallback text, and retirement notes. Stateful records are minimal, deterministic, migration-aware, and tested through focused round trips. UI copy names the action, cost, uncertainty, and irreversible consequence, with keyboard/controller focus and text alternatives. Performance is bounded by catalog parse, query, panel refresh, and long-text budgets; an optional content packet can be disabled without corrupting canonical state. The packet closes with a premise question, a source path to verify, a small input/output example, and a rollback boundary.

The fiction remains material and specific: soot in a seal groove, wet chalk under a glove, a meal cooling while two people argue, a lamp reflected in a chart, or a name written twice because both versions are true. That texture is connected to a mechanic, a location, a faction memory, or a consequence so the prose adds playable meaning. A scene can end in refusal, delay, repair, compromise, or a clean break; each result is legible and archived by the owner that actually changed. The packet must not claim the family story cards already exists, and it must stop if a current system or approved plan already owns the behavior.

Start with a current-source census: locate the owner, public API, catalog row, event producer, save section, host binding, and any existing plan claim. Define the player-facing loop in six beats: prepare, inspect, choose, commit, receive feedback, and decide what to do next. Give the packet one named mechanic, one location or shelter image, one character or faction voice, one failure state, and one late-game callback. Every packet is a proposal until its current owner, catalog reference, consumer, save seam, and host route are proven. It should state what the player sees, what can fail, and which existing fact is authoritative. It may enrich a journal, archive, radio, or epilogue surface, but it may not create a parallel ledger or a hidden authority. Candidate data uses schema_version, stable snake_case IDs, explicit references, localization keys, fallback text, and retirement notes. Stateful records are minimal, deterministic, migration-aware, and tested through focused round trips. UI copy names the action, cost, uncertainty, and irreversible consequence, with keyboard/controller focus and text alternatives. Performance is bounded by catalog parse, query, panel refresh, and long-text budgets; an optional content packet can be disabled without corrupting canonical state. The packet closes with a premise question, a source path to verify, a small input/output example, and a rollback boundary.

The fiction remains material and specific: soot in a seal groove, wet chalk under a glove, a meal cooling while two people argue, a lamp reflected in a chart, or a name written twice because both versions are true. That texture is connected to a mechanic, a location, a faction memory, or a consequence so the prose adds playable meaning. A scene can end in refusal, delay, repair, compromise, or a clean break; each result is legible and archived by the owner that actually changed. The packet must not claim the generational vocation notes already exists, and it must stop if a current system or approved plan already owns the behavior.

## Wave 3 dense-volume handoff

The ten deepening packets are ready for premise review as a high-volume authoring backlog. A builder should select one packet only after proving the current seam, then implement the smallest vertical slice with one canonical result, one visible route, one persistence or projection check, and one deterministic replay case where state changes. Writers may continue expanding the voice and location banks, but every new line needs a consumer, trigger, localization key, and archive policy.


## Continuation Wave 4 — Passes 32–42: Survivor Vocations, Personal Arcs, and Shelter Culture

This fourth synchronized tranche extends the ten existing fields with new mechanics, systems, locations, lore, character material, factions, and late-game consequences. Fields 11–20 remain deferred until this individual plan reaches 100,000 words. The material is documentation-only, premise-gated, and bounded by survivor roster, relationship and decay owners, skill progression, duty and needs systems, HobbySystem, SurvivorEducationSystem, ShelterArchiveSystem, and journal routing.

**Wave 4 provisional groups:** Hearth Circle, Ledgerhands, Dust Choir, Lantern Apprentices, Common Table, and the proposed Shelter Commons. **Wave 4 places:** Common Room, repair alcove, old classroom, meal line, memorial wall, north sleeping gallery.

### Dense packet 1: portfolio review

## Wave 4 micro-variant bank

These short records raise prose volume while keeping each addition reviewable and tied to an owner.

### Micro-variant 1: portfolio reflection variants

Portfolio reflection variants is a six-line variant family for the current Wave 4 content. This micro-bank supplies six short variants for calm, pressure, loss, recovery, refusal, and late arrival. Each line receives a localization key, speaker or surface, trigger, and fallback. The variant points to one existing mechanic or fact and names the consequence in plain language. It may change tone, public memory, or a next available choice, but it cannot mutate a second ledger. The writer keeps the material details close: a dry seal, a wet glove, a meal left under cloth, a lamp turned low, a tool returned, or a name spoken twice. The systems note identifies the canonical owner, the UI note identifies focus and text alternatives, and the verification note identifies one focused check and one reload case. It remains provisional until the source census proves that the referenced route, faction, survivor, location, archive, and save seams are live and unique.

## Twelve new story and side-quest packets

### Story packet 49: The Shelter Constitution

A rule about work leaves out care. The player can amend it, reject it, or ask the people doing care to write the clause. The packet needs entry condition, player choice, owner call, refusal or failure, archive fact, and late-arrival variant. Prose is a playable surface; it does not replace the mechanic, data contract, save behavior, or UI route.

### Story packet 50: Role Mediation

Two survivors both want the same duty for different reasons. The player helps them name what the duty means. The packet needs entry condition, player choice, owner call, refusal or failure, archive fact, and late-arrival variant. Prose is a playable surface; it does not replace the mechanic, data contract, save behavior, or UI route.

### Story packet 51: Learning Route

A classroom has stairs and no alternate path. The player chooses a route redesign that changes who can attend. The packet needs entry condition, player choice, owner call, refusal or failure, archive fact, and late-arrival variant. Prose is a playable surface; it does not replace the mechanic, data contract, save behavior, or UI route.

### Story packet 54: Festival Work

Prose is a playable surface; it does not replace the mechanic, data contract, save behavior, or UI route.

### Story packet 55: Repair and Reconciliation

A damaged tool is repaired before the argument is resolved. The player decides whether the repair is a bridge or merely useful. The packet needs entry condition, player choice, owner call, refusal or failure, archive fact, and late-arrival variant. Prose is a playable surface; it does not replace the mechanic, data contract, save behavior, or UI route.

### Story packet 56: Craft Credit

A child finishes a design started by an elder. The player chooses how both names appear. The packet needs entry condition, player choice, owner call, refusal or failure, archive fact, and late-arrival variant. Prose is a playable surface; it does not replace the mechanic, data contract, save behavior, or UI route.

### Story packet 57: Age Exchange

An elder learns a new route from a child. The player protects the exchange from becoming a performance. The packet needs entry condition, player choice, owner call, refusal or failure, archive fact, and late-arrival variant. Prose is a playable surface; it does not replace the mechanic, data contract, save behavior, or UI route.

### Story packet 58: Reframed Vocation

A survivor no longer wants the badge that saved them. The player helps name work that fits now. The packet needs entry condition, player choice, owner call, refusal or failure, archive fact, and late-arrival variant. Prose is a playable surface; it does not replace the mechanic, data contract, save behavior, or UI route.

The Commons writes a welcome rule with a blank line for the future. The player decides who may fill it. Prose is a playable surface; it does not replace the mechanic, data contract, save behavior, or UI route.

## Ten Wave 5 integration bridges

### Campaign bridge

Read current campaign flags and emit one named content fact; never add a second clock or victory state. The evidence packet includes one source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Faction bridge

Route consequences for Hearth Circle, Ledgerhands, Dust Choir, Lantern Apprentices, Common Table, and Shelter Commons through canonical standing or diplomacy after ID and alias review. The evidence packet includes one source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Relationship bridge

Read trust, affinity, grief, consent, and decay from existing survivor owners; a scene beat is not a relationship ledger. The evidence packet includes one source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Map/route bridge

Project Common Room, repair alcove, old classroom, meal line, memorial wall, north sleeping gallery onto current cartography, expedition, weather, vehicle, colony, and route seams rather than creating a parallel graph. The evidence packet includes one source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Shelter bridge

Use current facility, expansion, water, power, needs, duty, archive, celebration, and memorial owners. The evidence packet includes one source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Content bridge

Validate schema, IDs, localization keys, references, reachability, and retirement before adding volume. The evidence packet includes one source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Save bridge

Capture only non-recomputable progress or processed IDs in an existing owner and prove round trip. The evidence packet includes one source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Determinism bridge

Use keyed seeded inputs and stable ordering; paired replay must match outcomes and records after reload. The evidence packet includes one source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### UI bridge

Expose truthful state with focus, controller, text equivalents, disposal, and bounded loading; panels stay adapters. The evidence packet includes one source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Handoff bridge

Attach source paths, data examples, focused checks, performance notes, rollback, and unresolved decisions. The evidence packet includes one source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Pass 54: Shelter Identity Census

#### Canon and premise delta

This pass adds a new pressure point to the established scaffold. The premise audit must prove whether the meal already exists under another name before this proposal advances. Recheck current source, data, save ownership, host construction, and live ledger claims. Existing APIs and catalogs outrank this proposal. If a current owner supplies the behavior, retain this as content, projection, or presentation. The review names the smallest observable result and the evidence that would prove it. If source differs, keep the entry tagged as a proposal and stop instead of compensating with parallel authority. This keeps the design useful to writers, systems designers, UI implementers, and reviewers.

#### Player loop and decision pressure

This pass adds a new pressure point to the established scaffold. Use the memory as the player-facing review object and connect it to one of Fields 11–20 without inventing a new store. Describe preparation, inspection, commitment, feedback, and the next decision. Name cost and refusal. Use canonical day, resource, needs, travel, relationship, faction, and campaign facts rather than hidden local counters. The review names the smallest observable result and the evidence that would prove it. If source differs, keep the entry tagged as a proposal and stop instead of compensating with parallel authority. This keeps the design useful to writers, systems designers, UI implementers, and reviewers.

#### New mechanic and system rules

This pass adds a new pressure point to the established scaffold. The focal mechanic is shelter identity census derived from current roster and archive facts. Define inputs, thresholds, mutation owner, failure response, and visible feedback. State inputs, thresholds, evaluation order, consequence, no-provider behavior, and one mutation owner. Keyed seeded variation must be stable. Consumers receive facts and cannot become authorities. The review names the smallest observable result and the evidence that would prove it. If source differs, keep the entry tagged as a proposal and stop instead of compensating with parallel authority. This keeps the design useful to writers, systems designers, UI implementers, and reviewers.

#### Locations and shelter lore

This pass adds a new pressure point to the established scaffold. Anchor the scene in the badge: describe sound, material, work, hazard, shelter meaning, and map or facility seam. Give the place material texture, practical job, hazard, shelter relation, and memory. New IDs remain candidate POIs until map and facility owners confirm them. A vignette must lead to clue, choice, record, or route. The review names the smallest observable result and the evidence that would prove it. If source differs, keep the entry tagged as a proposal and stop instead of compensating with parallel authority. This keeps the design useful to writers, systems designers, UI implementers, and reviewers.

#### Character and faction continuity

This pass adds a new pressure point to the established scaffold. Give one character a reason to protect the lesson, another a reason to question it, and a faction a reason to remember it. Give each voice desire, limit, rhythm, and change. Read roster, relationship, standing, skill, memorial, and campaign facts. Proposed factions require alias and standing-sink checks. The review names the smallest observable result and the evidence that would prove it. If source differs, keep the entry tagged as a proposal and stop instead of compensating with parallel authority. This keeps the design useful to writers, systems designers, UI implementers, and reviewers.

#### Authored data and prose schema

This pass adds a new pressure point to the established scaffold. Candidate rows must name the room with stable IDs, trigger, references, fallback text, localization, and archive policy. Candidate rows need schema_version, snake_case ID, owner, prerequisites, references, effects, fallback text, localization key, archive policy, and retirement notes. High-volume rows reject dangling references. The review names the smallest observable result and the evidence that would prove it. If source differs, keep the entry tagged as a proposal and stop instead of compensating with parallel authority. This keeps the design useful to writers, systems designers, UI implementers, and reviewers.

#### Persistence and deterministic replay

This pass adds a new pressure point to the established scaffold. If the meal recurs, specify minimal progress or processed-event state and keyed replay inputs that prevent duplicates. Persist only non-recomputable progress and processed events in an existing owner. Specify capture, restore, migration, duplicate-event, rollback. Replay must agree on outcomes, records, order, and prose keys. The review names the smallest observable result and the evidence that would prove it. If source differs, keep the entry tagged as a proposal and stop instead of compensating with parallel authority. This keeps the design useful to writers, systems designers, UI implementers, and reviewers.

#### Host/UI/UX and performance

This pass adds a new pressure point to the established scaffold. The player must find the memory, understand state, navigate with keyboard/controller, and receive a safe fallback if data is absent or large. Expose truthful state with focus-safe keyboard/controller navigation, text alternatives, contrast, long-text behavior, disposal, and bounded query/load budgets. Panels stay adapters. The review names the smallest observable result and the evidence that would prove it. If source differs, keep the entry tagged as a proposal and stop instead of compensating with parallel authority. This keeps the design useful to writers, systems designers, UI implementers, and reviewers.

#### Storyline and side-quest consequences

This pass adds a new pressure point to the established scaffold. Stage a short scene around the promise, with a quiet prose beat, practical choice, and consequence routed through an existing owner. Every scene needs entry condition, choice, refusal or failure, concrete consequence, archive/journal fact, and late-arrival line. Keep prose restrained and sensory. The review names the smallest observable result and the evidence that would prove it. If source differs, keep the entry tagged as a proposal and stop instead of compensating with parallel authority. This keeps the design useful to writers, systems designers, UI implementers, and reviewers.

#### Verification and implementation handoff

This pass adds a new pressure point to the established scaffold. The acceptance packet must include a source path, input/output example involving the badge, unresolved question, and rollback boundary. Require premise evidence, focused data or contract checks, runtime smoke only when needed, save round trip, deterministic replay, performance notes, and rollback. A document is not implementation. The review names the smallest observable result and the evidence that would prove it. If source differs, keep the entry tagged as a proposal and stop instead of compensating with parallel authority. This keeps the design useful to writers, systems designers, UI implementers, and reviewers.

## Twelve new story and side-quest packets

### Story packet 61: Identity Census

The shelter census asks people to choose which name appears first. The player learns that accuracy and belonging can conflict. The packet needs entry condition, player choice, owner call, refusal or failure, archive fact, and late-arrival variant. Prose is a playable surface; it does not replace the mechanic, data contract, save behavior, or UI route.

A care signal is visible only from one room. The player redesigns it so help does not depend on knowing the right door. Prose is a playable surface; it does not replace the mechanic, data contract, save behavior, or UI route.

The Commons charter fails to include rest. The player can amend it, postpone, or proceed with the gap visible. ## Ten Wave 6 integration bridges

### Campaign bridge

Read current campaign flags and emit one named content fact; never add a second clock or victory state. The evidence packet includes one source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Faction bridge

Route consequences for Hearth Circle, Ledgerhands, Dust Choir, Lantern Apprentices, Common Table, and Shelter Commons through canonical standing or diplomacy after ID and alias review. The evidence packet includes one source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Relationship bridge

Read trust, affinity, grief, consent, and decay from existing survivor owners; a scene beat is not a relationship ledger. The evidence packet includes one source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Map/route bridge

Project Common Room, repair alcove, old classroom, meal line, memorial wall, north sleeping gallery onto current cartography, expedition, weather, vehicle, colony, and route seams rather than creating a parallel graph. The evidence packet includes one source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Shelter bridge

Use current facility, expansion, water, power, needs, duty, archive, celebration, and memorial owners. The evidence packet includes one source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Content bridge

Validate schema, IDs, localization keys, references, reachability, and retirement before adding volume. The evidence packet includes one source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Save bridge

Capture only non-recomputable progress or processed IDs in an existing owner and prove round trip. The evidence packet includes one source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Determinism bridge

Use keyed seeded inputs and stable ordering; paired replay must match outcomes and records after reload. The evidence packet includes one source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### UI bridge

Expose truthful state with focus, controller, text equivalents, disposal, and bounded loading; panels stay adapters. The evidence packet includes one source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Handoff bridge

Attach source paths, data examples, focused checks, performance notes, rollback, and unresolved decisions. The evidence packet includes one source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

Select one focal mechanic, one place or shelter memory, one character or faction voice, one player command or read projection, one journal/archive result, one post-100k field, and one save/replay fixture. ## Ten Wave 7 integration bridges

### Campaign bridge

Read current campaign flags and emit one named content fact; never add a second clock or victory state. The evidence packet includes one source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Faction bridge

Route consequences for Hearth Circle, Ledgerhands, Dust Choir, Lantern Apprentices, Common Table, and Shelter Commons through canonical standing or diplomacy after ID and alias review. The evidence packet includes one source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Relationship bridge

Read trust, affinity, grief, consent, and decay from existing survivor owners; a scene beat is not a relationship ledger. The evidence packet includes one source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Map/route bridge

Project Common Room, repair alcove, old classroom, meal line, memorial wall, north sleeping gallery onto current cartography, expedition, weather, vehicle, colony, and route seams rather than creating a parallel graph. The evidence packet includes one source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Shelter bridge

Use current facility, expansion, water, power, needs, duty, archive, celebration, and memorial owners. The evidence packet includes one source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Content bridge

Validate schema, IDs, localization keys, references, reachability, and retirement before adding volume. The evidence packet includes one source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Save bridge

Capture only non-recomputable progress or processed IDs in an existing owner and prove round trip. The evidence packet includes one source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Determinism bridge

Use keyed seeded inputs and stable ordering; paired replay must match outcomes and records after reload. The evidence packet includes one source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### UI bridge

Expose truthful state with focus, controller, text equivalents, disposal, and bounded loading; panels stay adapters. The evidence packet includes one source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Handoff bridge

Attach source paths, data examples, focused checks, performance notes, rollback, and unresolved decisions. The evidence packet includes one source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Volume packet 01: The Baker’s Inventory

This dense Wave 7 continuation packet extends Shelter culture through a contested promise and a choice between public repair, private repair, or a principled refusal. It is deliberately additive: it does not create another field layer after Fields 11–20, and it does not claim that a provisional faction, location, mechanic, or prose record exists in production.

Place the first clue near a practical tool: a pump handle, route chalk, ration tin, needle, relay key, or ledger clasp. The object teaches the mechanic through use.

The playable beat begins with a short observation at the shelter culture seam. A resident asks a question that cannot be answered by a tooltip alone. The player can inspect the evidence, ask for the practical need, compare two records, or leave the matter untouched. Inspection grants context; asking exposes a cost; comparison reveals a mismatch; leaving preserves uncertainty. The command must be represented by an existing owner event and must emit a fact that later systems can consume without reading panel state.

The scene then crosses three scales. At shelter scale, one room or work area changes its arrangement and writes a small archive or journal result. At faction scale, one representative revises a stance, makes a concession, or names a boundary. At late-game scale, the same fact appears as a route, legacy, coalition, or ending input. These projections are read-only views of canonical state. They must degrade gracefully when the optional record is missing and must never invent a favorable outcome merely to complete the prose.

Character direction for this packet: the practical resident speaks in short sentences, notices tools before symbols, and offers help without promising safety. The faction voice uses formal language until challenged by a concrete shortage. A third voice, perhaps a courier, apprentice, witness, or absent person represented by an object, reframes the conflict. Their personalities are differentiated through choices and timing rather than accent caricature. Give each voice a refusal that can be respected and a late callback that acknowledges the player’s earlier decision.

Location and shelter lore should answer who built the space, what failed, who repaired it, what rule grew from that repair, and what the rule costs now. Use one physical trace, one remembered phrase, one disputed interpretation, and one maintenance task. The place becomes more than a backdrop because the player can act there, return there, and observe a consequence there. Do not duplicate a named location: run a catalog and alias check and fold into an existing record if the premise is already covered.

Mechanic acceptance for The Baker’s Inventory: a focused owner check proves the command and event; a save round trip proves capture and restore; a paired seeded replay proves order and result; a bounded host smoke proves the projection; and a UI review proves focus, close/back, contrast, text scaling, and long-copy behavior. Performance review records catalog parse, query, refresh, and archive costs. The rollback note identifies the event key, record IDs, migration boundary, and prose keys that can be removed without orphaning live state.

The packet closes with a quiet image: place the first clue near a practical tool: a pump handle, route chalk, ration tin, needle, relay key, or ledger clasp. the object teaches the mechanic through use. The image is not a reward screen. It is a check that the player’s choice has entered the world’s ordinary labor. If the source owner, data schema, or current integration plan disagrees with this proposal, retain the packet as a bounded question and stop at the premise audit rather than creating a parallel system.

## Continuation Wave 8 — Passes 76–86

This synchronized continuation keeps Fields 11–20 active. It adds new provisional factions, late-game organizations, locations, shelter customs, survivor voices, mechanics, side quests, UI/UX scaffolds, and performance or replay gates without claiming production implementation or creating parallel mutable state.


### Pass 76: The Rainline Lesson

This pass extends shelter culture and survivor vocations with the rainline lesson. It is a proposal over the current authority owned by roster, relationship, skills, duty, needs, HobbySystem, SurvivorEducationSystem, ShelterArchiveSystem, and journal owners. The named factions and places are provisional labels, not catalog facts. Start with a source, data, consumer, and ownership audit; if an existing record already expresses the idea, fold this material into that record or stop. The player should make a legible choice that affects a practical task, a remembered relationship, a route, or a late-game interpretation.

#### 1. Premise evidence

Record the exact source path, API or JSON family, event producer, host route, and current plan entry that justify the rainline lesson. Name one absent seam and one collision to check. A proposal remains tagged unresolved until the premise is reproduced against current source.

#### 2. Owner contract

Route the command through roster, relationship, skills, duty, needs, HobbySystem, SurvivorEducationSystem, ShelterArchiveSystem, and journal owners. These packets add volume to the current Wave 10 fields without introducing Fields 21–30. Each is a bounded design record for story, mechanics, systems, locations, shelter lore, character personalities, factions, late-game pressure, UI, persistence, replay, and performance.


### Supplemental packet 01: shelter culture and survivor vocations — Copper Meridian Classroom action 1

The scene opens at **Copper Meridian Classroom**, where the practical detail is more urgent than the ceremonial language: a damp ledger, a half-full water drum, a frayed coat, a relay key, a route marker, or an unlit lamp. A resident asks the player to inspect the public ledger. The player sees the cost before accepting and can refuse without losing the ability to return. The first response creates one canonical event and one journal or archive projection; later content reads that fact through the existing owner rather than through a panel cache.

**Mechanic and system contract.** Define the input, command, event key, result, refusal, fallback, and next choice. Use existing campaign, faction, relationship, roster, expedition, shelter, archive, or ending authority as appropriate. Stateful effects use the smallest current save section with capture, restore, migration, duplicate-event handling, and a seeded replay fixture. Do not create a second reputation score, route graph, relationship network, inventory ledger, calendar, or ending state. If the premise is absent in current source or data, keep this packet unresolved and record the exact missing seam.

**Location and shelter lore.** Explain who built Copper Meridian Classroom, what failed there, who repaired it, what custom grew from that repair, and who still pays its cost. Give the player one physical trace, one remembered phrase, one disputed interpretation, and one maintenance task. On a return visit, show the consequence before dialogue summarizes it. A quiet shelter detail should carry history: a bed rotated away from a draft, a cup reserved for visitors, a chalk line refreshed after rain, or a tool returned sharper than it was found.

**Character and faction direction.** The resident speaks plainly and notices labor before symbolism. A witness from **Copper Meridian Tutors** uses formal language until a shortage makes the stakes concrete. A third voice may be an apprentice, courier, absent person represented by an object, or elder who remembers a different version. Give each a promise, fear, boundary, apology, refusal, and late callback. Let a minor voice receive one measurable outcome in the roster, route, archive, relationship, or ending projection.

**Story, UI, and verification.** The side quest needs an entry condition, player action, cost, consequence, refusal branch, archive fact, late-arrival variant, and missing-record variant. Prose should reveal the mechanic through ordinary work. The UI needs a compact label, expanded explanation, focus order, keyboard/controller close and back, readable long text, contrast, non-color cues, and confirmation for irreversible actions. Acceptance requires premise evidence, owner and consumer proof, focused contract or data checks, save round trip, paired deterministic replay, performance notes, and a rollback boundary. The first response creates one canonical event and one journal or archive projection; later content reads that fact through the existing owner rather than through a panel cache.

**Mechanic and system contract.** Define the input, command, event key, result, refusal, fallback, and next choice. Use existing campaign, faction, relationship, roster, expedition, shelter, archive, or ending authority as appropriate. Stateful effects use the smallest current save section with capture, restore, migration, duplicate-event handling, and a seeded replay fixture. Do not create a second reputation score, route graph, relationship network, inventory ledger, calendar, or ending state. If the premise is absent in current source or data, keep this packet unresolved and record the exact missing seam.

**Location and shelter lore.** Explain who built Fallowlight Commons, what failed there, who repaired it, what custom grew from that repair, and who still pays its cost. Give the player one physical trace, one remembered phrase, one disputed interpretation, and one maintenance task. On a return visit, show the consequence before dialogue summarizes it. A quiet shelter detail should carry history: a bed rotated away from a draft, a cup reserved for visitors, a chalk line refreshed after rain, or a tool returned sharper than it was found.

**Character and faction direction.** The resident speaks plainly and notices labor before symbolism. A witness from **Fallowlight Makers** uses formal language until a shortage makes the stakes concrete. A third voice may be an apprentice, courier, absent person represented by an object, or elder who remembers a different version. Give each a promise, fear, boundary, apology, refusal, and late callback. Let a minor voice receive one measurable outcome in the roster, route, archive, relationship, or ending projection.

**Story, UI, and verification.** The side quest needs an entry condition, player action, cost, consequence, refusal branch, archive fact, late-arrival variant, and missing-record variant. Prose should reveal the mechanic through ordinary work. The UI needs a compact label, expanded explanation, focus order, keyboard/controller close and back, readable long text, contrast, non-color cues, and confirmation for irreversible actions. Acceptance requires premise evidence, owner and consumer proof, focused contract or data checks, save round trip, paired deterministic replay, performance notes, and a rollback boundary. The packet is not an implementation claim; it is ready only for a safe-slice review.

### Pass 131: The Cinderwake Lesson

This pass extends shelter culture and survivor vocations with the cinderwake lesson. It is a proposal over the current authority owned by roster, relationship, skills, duty, needs, HobbySystem, SurvivorEducationSystem, ShelterArchiveSystem, and journal owners. The named factions and places are provisional labels, not catalog facts. Start with a source, data, consumer, and ownership audit; if an existing record already expresses the idea, fold this material into that record or stop. The player should make a legible choice that affects a practical task, a remembered relationship, a route, or a late-game interpretation.

#### 1. Premise evidence

Record the exact source path, API or JSON family, event producer, host route, and current plan entry that justify the cinderwake lesson. Name one absent seam and one collision to check. A proposal remains tagged unresolved until the premise is reproduced against current source.

#### 2. Owner contract

Route the command through roster, relationship, skills, duty, needs, HobbySystem, SurvivorEducationSystem, ShelterArchiveSystem, and journal owners. Define the input, output, refusal, fallback, and event key. Panels, maps, and prose consume the projection and never become a second ledger, graph, clock, route registry, roster, or ending resolver.

#### 3. Player action

Give the player inspect, ask, compare, repair, invite, ration, disclose, wait, or leave choices around the cinderwake lesson. Show cost before commitment, allow a respectful refusal, and provide recovery work or information after a failure unless the canonical owner defines a terminal outcome.

#### 4. State and save

Use the smallest existing save section. Capture and restore the new fact, migrate older envelopes, make duplicate events idempotent, and keep optional content safe when its record is absent. Do not add a local counter merely to make the prose conditional.

#### 5. Deterministic replay

Pin a seeded event key, input order, and expected result. A paired replay must produce the same standing, route, roster, archive, or ending projection. Avoid wall-clock seeds, unordered iteration, and hidden random choices in authored content.

#### 6. Location and shelter projection

#### 7. Character and faction voice

#### 8. Story and side-quest result

Build a side quest from an entry fact, one player action, one cost, one consequence, one refusal, one archive or journal fact, and a late-arrival variant. The scene may use prose, but the quest result must be an observable owner event that later content can read.

#### 9. UI and accessibility

#### 10. Performance and rollback

#### 10. Performance and rollback

Set budgets for catalog parse, query, event dispatch, panel refresh, archive projection, and long text. Include a missing-data path, a rollback boundary, a focused contract check, a save round trip, and a host smoke only where the owner route requires it.
**Pass 140 receipt.** Accept A Skill for Thin Fuel only when the owner, player result, failure behavior, save/replay fixture, and rollback note are written.
