If that action cannot be wired to current authority, keep the packet as a design question.


### Pass 141: The Repaired Name

This pass extends shelter culture and survivor vocations with the repaired name. It is a proposal over the current authority owned by roster, relationship, skills, duty, needs, HobbySystem, SurvivorEducationSystem, ShelterArchiveSystem, and journal owners. The named factions and places are provisional labels, not catalog facts. Start with a source, data, consumer, and ownership audit; if an existing record already expresses the idea, fold this material into that record or stop. The player should make a legible choice that affects a practical task, a remembered relationship, a route, or a late-game interpretation.

#### 1. Premise evidence

Record the exact source path, API or JSON family, event producer, host route, and current plan entry that justify the repaired name. Name one absent seam and one collision to check. A proposal remains tagged unresolved until the premise is reproduced against current source.

#### 2. Owner contract

Route the command through roster, relationship, skills, duty, needs, HobbySystem, SurvivorEducationSystem, ShelterArchiveSystem, and journal owners. Define the input, output, refusal, fallback, and event key. Panels, maps, and prose consume the projection and never become a second ledger, graph, clock, route registry, roster, or ending resolver.

#### 3. Player action

Give the player inspect, ask, compare, repair, invite, ration, disclose, wait, or leave choices around the repaired name. Show cost before commitment, allow a respectful refusal, and provide recovery work or information after a failure unless the canonical owner defines a terminal outcome.

#### 4. State and save

Use the smallest existing save section. Capture and restore the new fact, migrate older envelopes, make duplicate events idempotent, and keep optional content safe when its record is absent. Do not add a local counter merely to make the prose conditional.

#### 5. Deterministic replay

Pin a seeded event key, input order, and expected result. A paired replay must produce the same standing, route, roster, archive, or ending projection. Avoid wall-clock seeds, unordered iteration, and hidden random choices in authored content.

#### 6. Location and shelter projection

Stage arrival, inspection, work, hazard, rest, departure, and return at Pale River Classroom. Add one physical trace, one shelter custom, one disputed memory, and one maintenance task so the location carries lore through action rather than exposition alone.

#### 7. Character and faction voice

Write distinct voices for a practical resident, an affected witness, and one representative of Pale River Tutors. Give each a promise, fear, boundary, refusal, apology, and late callback. Let a minor or absent voice receive a measurable consequence.

#### 8. Story and side-quest result

Build a side quest from an entry fact, one player action, one cost, one consequence, one refusal, one archive or journal fact, and a late-arrival variant. The scene may use prose, but the quest result must be an observable owner event that later content can read.

#### 9. UI and accessibility

Provide concise labels, expanded explanations, focus order, keyboard and controller back behavior, contrast, text scaling, non-color cues, irreversible-action confirmation, and a text or audio alternative. Long records must page or collapse without hiding the consequence.

#### 10. Performance and rollback

Set budgets for catalog parse, query, event dispatch, panel refresh, archive projection, and long text. Include a missing-data path, a rollback boundary, a focused contract check, a save round trip, and a host smoke only where the owner route requires it.
**Pass 141 receipt.** Accept The Repaired Name only when the owner, player result, failure behavior, save/replay fixture, and rollback note are written. The prose beat ends with an ordinary action: a lamp is trimmed, a pump is checked, a meal is shared, a coat is mended, a route marker is moved, or a record is read aloud. ## Wave 13 closeout receipt

The Wave 13 material remains documentation-only. Promotion requires current-source premise evidence, owner and consumer proof, reachable data, deterministic save and replay fixtures, UI/accessibility review, performance notes, and a rollback boundary.

## Wave 13 supplemental depth packets

These packets add volume to the current Wave 13 fields without introducing Fields 21–30. Each is a bounded design record for story, mechanics, systems, locations, shelter lore, character personalities, factions, late-game pressure, UI, persistence, replay, and performance.


### Supplemental packet 01: shelter culture and survivor vocations — Pale River Classroom action 1

The scene opens at **Pale River Classroom**, where the practical detail is more urgent than the ceremonial language: a damp ledger, a half-full water drum, a frayed coat, a relay key, a route marker, or an unlit lamp. A resident asks the player to inspect the public ledger. The player sees the cost before accepting and can refuse without losing the ability to return. The first response creates one canonical event and one journal or archive projection; later content reads that fact through the existing owner rather than through a panel cache.

**Mechanic and system contract.** Define the input, command, event key, result, refusal, fallback, and next choice. Use existing campaign, faction, relationship, roster, expedition, shelter, archive, or ending authority as appropriate. Stateful effects use the smallest current save section with capture, restore, migration, duplicate-event handling, and a seeded replay fixture. Do not create a second reputation score, route graph, relationship network, inventory ledger, calendar, or ending state. If the premise is absent in current source or data, keep this packet unresolved and record the exact missing seam.

**Location and shelter lore.** Explain who built Pale River Classroom, what failed there, who repaired it, what custom grew from that repair, and who still pays its cost. ### Supplemental packet 01: shelter culture and survivor vocations — Copper Finch Classroom action 1

The scene opens at **Copper Finch Classroom**, where the practical detail is more urgent than the ceremonial language: a damp ledger, a half-full water drum, a frayed coat, a relay key, a route marker, or an unlit lamp. A resident asks the player to inspect the public ledger. The player sees the cost before accepting and can refuse without losing the ability to return. The first response creates one canonical event and one journal or archive projection; later content reads that fact through the existing owner rather than through a panel cache.

**Mechanic and system contract.** Define the input, command, event key, result, refusal, fallback, and next choice. Use existing campaign, faction, relationship, roster, expedition, shelter, archive, or ending authority as appropriate. Stateful effects use the smallest current save section with capture, restore, migration, duplicate-event handling, and a seeded replay fixture. Do not create a second reputation score, route graph, relationship network, inventory ledger, calendar, or ending state. If the premise is absent in current source or data, keep this packet unresolved and record the exact missing seam.

**Location and shelter lore.** Explain who built Copper Finch Classroom, what failed there, who repaired it, what custom grew from that repair, and who still pays its cost. Give the player one physical trace, one remembered phrase, one disputed interpretation, and one maintenance task. On a return visit, show the consequence before dialogue summarizes it. A quiet shelter detail should carry history: a bed rotated away from a draft, a cup reserved for visitors, a chalk line refreshed after rain, or a tool returned sharper than it was found.

**Character and faction direction.** The resident speaks plainly and notices labor before symbolism. A witness from **Copper Finch Tutors** uses formal language until a shortage makes the stakes concrete. A third voice may be an apprentice, courier, absent person represented by an object, or elder who remembers a different version. Give each a promise, fear, boundary, apology, refusal, and late callback. Let a minor voice receive one measurable outcome in the roster, route, archive, relationship, or ending projection.

**Story, UI, and verification.** The side quest needs an entry condition, player action, cost, consequence, refusal branch, archive fact, late-arrival variant, and missing-record variant. Prose should reveal the mechanic through ordinary work. The UI needs a compact label, expanded explanation, focus order, keyboard/controller close and back, readable long text, contrast, non-color cues, and confirmation for irreversible actions. Acceptance requires premise evidence, owner and consumer proof, focused contract or data checks, save round trip, paired deterministic replay, performance notes, and a rollback boundary. Prose should reveal the mechanic through ordinary work. The UI needs a compact label, expanded explanation, focus order, keyboard/controller close and back, readable long text, contrast, non-color cues, and confirmation for irreversible actions. Acceptance requires premise evidence, owner and consumer proof, focused contract or data checks, save round trip, paired deterministic replay, performance notes, and a rollback boundary. The packet is not an implementation claim; it is ready only for a safe-slice review.

Give the player inspect, ask, compare, repair, invite, ration, disclose, wait, or leave choices around the rebound name. Show cost before commitment, allow a respectful refusal, and provide recovery work or information after a failure unless the canonical owner defines a terminal outcome.

#### 4. State and save

Use the smallest existing save section. Capture and restore the new fact, migrate older envelopes, make duplicate events idempotent, and keep optional content safe when its record is absent. Do not add a local counter merely to make the prose conditional.

#### 5. Deterministic replay

Pin a seeded event key, input order, and expected result. A paired replay must produce the same standing, route, roster, archive, or ending projection. Avoid wall-clock seeds, unordered iteration, and hidden random choices in authored content.

#### 6. Location and shelter projection

Stage arrival, inspection, work, hazard, rest, departure, and return at White Basin Commons. Add one physical trace, one shelter custom, one disputed memory, and one maintenance task so the location carries lore through action rather than exposition alone.

#### 7. Character and faction voice

Write distinct voices for a practical resident, an affected witness, and one representative of White Basin Makers. Give each a promise, fear, boundary, refusal, apology, and late callback. Let a minor or absent voice receive a measurable consequence.

#### 8. Story and side-quest result

Build a side quest from an entry fact, one player action, one cost, one consequence, one refusal, one archive or journal fact, and a late-arrival variant. The scene may use prose, but the quest result must be an observable owner event that later content can read.

#### 9. UI and accessibility

Provide concise labels, expanded explanations, focus order, keyboard and controller back behavior, contrast, text scaling, non-color cues, irreversible-action confirmation, and a text or audio alternative. Long records must page or collapse without hiding the consequence.

#### 10. Performance and rollback

Set budgets for catalog parse, query, event dispatch, panel refresh, archive projection, and long text. Include a missing-data path, a rollback boundary, a focused contract check, a save round trip, and a host smoke only where the owner route requires it.
**Pass 196 receipt.** Accept The Rebound Name only when the owner, player result, failure behavior, save/replay fixture, and rollback note are written. The prose beat ends with an ordinary action: a lamp is trimmed, a pump is checked, a meal is shared, a coat is mended, a route marker is moved, or a record is read aloud. If that action cannot be wired to current authority, keep the packet as a design question.

## Wave 18 closeout receipt

The Wave 18 material remains documentation-only. Promotion requires current-source premise evidence, owner and consumer proof, reachable data, deterministic save and replay fixtures, UI/accessibility review, performance notes, and a rollback boundary.

## Wave 18 supplemental depth packets

These packets add volume to the current Wave 18 fields without introducing Fields 21–30. Each is a bounded design record for story, mechanics, systems, locations, shelter lore, character personalities, factions, late-game pressure, UI, persistence, replay, and performance.


### Supplemental packet 01: shelter culture and survivor vocations — Larkspur Classroom action 1

The scene opens at **Larkspur Classroom**, where the practical detail is more urgent than the ceremonial language: a damp ledger, a half-full water drum, a frayed coat, a relay key, a route marker, or an unlit lamp. A resident asks the player to inspect the public ledger. The player sees the cost before accepting and can refuse without losing the ability to return. The first response creates one canonical event and one journal or archive projection; later content reads that fact through the existing owner rather than through a panel cache.

**Mechanic and system contract.** Define the input, command, event key, result, refusal, fallback, and next choice. Use existing campaign, faction, relationship, roster, expedition, shelter, archive, or ending authority as appropriate. Stateful effects use the smallest current save section with capture, restore, migration, duplicate-event handling, and a seeded replay fixture. Do not create a second reputation score, route graph, relationship network, inventory ledger, calendar, or ending state. If the premise is absent in current source or data, keep this packet unresolved and record the exact missing seam.

**Location and shelter lore.** Explain who built Larkspur Classroom, what failed there, who repaired it, what custom grew from that repair, and who still pays its cost. Give the player one physical trace, one remembered phrase, one disputed interpretation, and one maintenance task. On a return visit, show the consequence before dialogue summarizes it. A quiet shelter detail should carry history: a bed rotated away from a draft, a cup reserved for visitors, a chalk line refreshed after rain, or a tool returned sharper than it was found.

**Character and faction direction.** The resident speaks plainly and notices labor before symbolism. A witness from **Larkspur Tutors** uses formal language until a shortage makes the stakes concrete. A third voice may be an apprentice, courier, absent person represented by an object, or elder who remembers a different version. Give each a promise, fear, boundary, apology, refusal, and late callback. Let a minor voice receive one measurable outcome in the roster, route, archive, relationship, or ending projection.

**Story, UI, and verification.** The side quest needs an entry condition, player action, cost, consequence, refusal branch, archive fact, late-arrival variant, and missing-record variant. Prose should reveal the mechanic through ordinary work. The UI needs a compact label, expanded explanation, focus order, keyboard/controller close and back, readable long text, contrast, non-color cues, and confirmation for irreversible actions. Acceptance requires premise evidence, owner and consumer proof, focused contract or data checks, save round trip, paired deterministic replay, performance notes, and a rollback boundary. The packet is not an implementation claim; it is ready only for a safe-slice review.

### Supplemental packet 01: shelter culture and survivor vocations — Penny Reed Classroom action 1

The scene opens at **Penny Reed Classroom**, where the practical detail is more urgent than the ceremonial language: a damp ledger, a half-full water drum, a frayed coat, a relay key, a route marker, or an unlit lamp. A resident asks the player to inspect the public ledger. The player sees the cost before accepting and can refuse without losing the ability to return. The first response creates one canonical event and one journal or archive projection; later content reads that fact through the existing owner rather than through a panel cache.

A quiet shelter detail should carry history: a bed rotated away from a draft, a cup reserved for visitors, a chalk line refreshed after rain, or a tool returned sharper than it was found.

Stage arrival, inspection, work, hazard, rest, departure, and return at North Candle Meal Hall. Add one physical trace, one shelter custom, one disputed memory, and one maintenance task so the location carries lore through action rather than exposition alone.

#### 7. Character and faction voice

Write distinct voices for a practical resident, an affected witness, and one representative of North Candle Storykeepers. Give each a promise, fear, boundary, refusal, apology, and late callback. Let a minor or absent voice receive a measurable consequence.

#### 8. Story and side-quest result

Build a side quest from an entry fact, one player action, one cost, one consequence, one refusal, one archive or journal fact, and a late-arrival variant. The scene may use prose, but the quest result must be an observable owner event that later content can read.

#### 9. UI and accessibility

Provide concise labels, expanded explanations, focus order, keyboard and controller back behavior, contrast, text scaling, non-color cues, irreversible-action confirmation, and a text or audio alternative. Long records must page or collapse without hiding the consequence.

#### 10. Performance and rollback

Set budgets for catalog parse, query, event dispatch, panel refresh, archive projection, and long text. Include a missing-data path, a rollback boundary, a focused contract check, a save round trip, and a host smoke only where the owner route requires it.
**Pass 251 receipt.** Accept The Recast Name only when the owner, player result, failure behavior, save/replay fixture, and rollback note are written. The prose beat ends with an ordinary action: a lamp is trimmed, a pump is checked, a meal is shared, a coat is mended, a route marker is moved, or a record is read aloud. If that action cannot be wired to current authority, keep the packet as a design question.

## Wave 23 closeout receipt

The Wave 23 material remains documentation-only. Promotion requires current-source premise evidence, owner and consumer proof, reachable data, deterministic save and replay fixtures, UI/accessibility review, performance notes, and a rollback boundary.

## Wave 23 supplemental depth packets

These packets add volume to the current Wave 23 fields without introducing Fields 21–30. Each is a bounded design record for story, mechanics, systems, locations, shelter lore, character personalities, factions, late-game pressure, UI, persistence, replay, and performance.


### Supplemental packet 01: shelter culture and survivor vocations — Copper Kestrel Classroom action 1

The scene opens at **Copper Kestrel Classroom**, where the practical detail is more urgent than the ceremonial language: a damp ledger, a half-full water drum, a frayed coat, a relay key, a route marker, or an unlit lamp. A resident asks the player to inspect the public ledger. The player sees the cost before accepting and can refuse without losing the ability to return. The first response creates one canonical event and one journal or archive projection; later content reads that fact through the existing owner rather than through a panel cache.

**Mechanic and system contract.** Define the input, command, event key, result, refusal, fallback, and next choice. Use existing campaign, faction, relationship, roster, expedition, shelter, archive, or ending authority as appropriate. Stateful effects use the smallest current save section with capture, restore, migration, duplicate-event handling, and a seeded replay fixture. Do not create a second reputation score, route graph, relationship network, inventory ledger, calendar, or ending state. If the premise is absent in current source or data, keep this packet unresolved and record the exact missing seam.

**Location and shelter lore.** Explain who built Copper Kestrel Classroom, what failed there, who repaired it, what custom grew from that repair, and who still pays its cost. Give the player one physical trace, one remembered phrase, one disputed interpretation, and one maintenance task. On a return visit, show the consequence before dialogue summarizes it. A quiet shelter detail should carry history: a bed rotated away from a draft, a cup reserved for visitors, a chalk line refreshed after rain, or a tool returned sharper than it was found.

**Character and faction direction.** The resident speaks plainly and notices labor before symbolism. A witness from **Copper Kestrel Tutors** uses formal language until a shortage makes the stakes concrete. A third voice may be an apprentice, courier, absent person represented by an object, or elder who remembers a different version. Give each a promise, fear, boundary, apology, refusal, and late callback. Let a minor voice receive one measurable outcome in the roster, route, archive, relationship, or ending projection.

**Story, UI, and verification.** The side quest needs an entry condition, player action, cost, consequence, refusal branch, archive fact, late-arrival variant, and missing-record variant. Prose should reveal the mechanic through ordinary work. The UI needs a compact label, expanded explanation, focus order, keyboard/controller close and back, readable long text, contrast, non-color cues, and confirmation for irreversible actions. Acceptance requires premise evidence, owner and consumer proof, focused contract or data checks, save round trip, paired deterministic replay, performance notes, and a rollback boundary. The packet is not an implementation claim; it is ready only for a safe-slice review.

## Wave 28 closeout receipt

The Wave 28 material remains documentation-only. Promotion requires current-source premise evidence, owner and consumer proof, reachable data, deterministic save and replay fixtures, UI/accessibility review, performance notes, and a rollback boundary.

## Wave 28 supplemental depth packets

These packets add volume to the current Wave 28 fields without introducing Fields 21–30. Each is a bounded design record for story, mechanics, systems, locations, shelter lore, character personalities, factions, late-game pressure, UI, persistence, replay, and performance.


### Supplemental packet 01: shelter culture and survivor vocations — Ochre Kite Classroom action 1

The scene opens at **Ochre Kite Classroom**, where the practical detail is more urgent than the ceremonial language: a damp ledger, a half-full water drum, a frayed coat, a relay key, a route marker, or an unlit lamp. A resident asks the player to inspect the public ledger. The player sees the cost before accepting and can refuse without losing the ability to return. The first response creates one canonical event and one journal or archive projection; later content reads that fact through the existing owner rather than through a panel cache.

**Mechanic and system contract.** Define the input, command, event key, result, refusal, fallback, and next choice. Use existing campaign, faction, relationship, roster, expedition, shelter, archive, or ending authority as appropriate. Stateful effects use the smallest current save section with capture, restore, migration, duplicate-event handling, and a seeded replay fixture. Do not create a second reputation score, route graph, relationship network, inventory ledger, calendar, or ending state. If the premise is absent in current source or data, keep this packet unresolved and record the exact missing seam.

**Location and shelter lore.** Explain who built Ochre Kite Classroom, what failed there, who repaired it, what custom grew from that repair, and who still pays its cost. Give the player one physical trace, one remembered phrase, one disputed interpretation, and one maintenance task. On a return visit, show the consequence before dialogue summarizes it. A quiet shelter detail should carry history: a bed rotated away from a draft, a cup reserved for visitors, a chalk line refreshed after rain, or a tool returned sharper than it was found.

**Character and faction direction.** The resident speaks plainly and notices labor before symbolism. A witness from **Ochre Kite Tutors** uses formal language until a shortage makes the stakes concrete. A third voice may be an apprentice, courier, absent person represented by an object, or elder who remembers a different version. Give each a promise, fear, boundary, apology, refusal, and late callback. Let a minor voice receive one measurable outcome in the roster, route, archive, relationship, or ending projection.

**Story, UI, and verification.** The side quest needs an entry condition, player action, cost, consequence, refusal branch, archive fact, late-arrival variant, and missing-record variant. Prose should reveal the mechanic through ordinary work. The UI needs a compact label, expanded explanation, focus order, keyboard/controller close and back, readable long text, contrast, non-color cues, and confirmation for irreversible actions. Acceptance requires premise evidence, owner and consumer proof, focused contract or data checks, save round trip, paired deterministic replay, performance notes, and a rollback boundary. The packet is not an implementation claim; it is ready only for a safe-slice review.

### Pass 329: The Dawnrush Lesson

This pass extends shelter culture and survivor vocations with the dawnrush lesson. It is a proposal over the current authority owned by roster, relationship, skills, duty, needs, HobbySystem, SurvivorEducationSystem, ShelterArchiveSystem, and journal owners. The named factions and places are provisional labels, not catalog facts. Start with a source, data, consumer, and ownership audit; if an existing record already expresses the idea, fold this material into that record or stop. The player should make a legible choice that affects a practical task, a remembered relationship, a route, or a late-game interpretation.

#### 1. Premise evidence

Record the exact source path, API or JSON family, event producer, host route, and current plan entry that justify the dawnrush lesson. Name one absent seam and one collision to check. A proposal remains tagged unresolved until the premise is reproduced against current source.

#### 2. Owner contract

Route the command through roster, relationship, skills, duty, needs, HobbySystem, SurvivorEducationSystem, ShelterArchiveSystem, and journal owners. Define the input, output, refusal, fallback, and event key. Panels, maps, and prose consume the projection and never become a second ledger, graph, clock, route registry, roster, or ending resolver.

#### 3. Player action

Give the player inspect, ask, compare, repair, invite, ration, disclose, wait, or leave choices around the dawnrush lesson. Show cost before commitment, allow a respectful refusal, and provide recovery work or information after a failure unless the canonical owner defines a terminal outcome.

#### 4. State and save

Use the smallest existing save section. Capture and restore the new fact, migrate older envelopes, make duplicate events idempotent, and keep optional content safe when its record is absent. Do not add a local counter merely to make the prose conditional.

#### 5. Deterministic replay

Pin a seeded event key, input order, and expected result. A paired replay must produce the same standing, route, roster, archive, or ending projection. Avoid wall-clock seeds, unordered iteration, and hidden random choices in authored content.

#### 6. Location and shelter projection

Stage arrival, inspection, work, hazard, rest, departure, and return at Olive Crane Classroom. Add one physical trace, one shelter custom, one disputed memory, and one maintenance task so the location carries lore through action rather than exposition alone.

#### 7. Character and faction voice

### Supplemental packet 01: shelter culture and survivor vocations — Olive Crane Classroom action 1

### Supplemental packet 01: shelter culture and survivor vocations — Cedar Lantern Classroom action 1

The scene opens at **Cedar Lantern Classroom**, where the practical detail is more urgent than the ceremonial language: a damp ledger, a half-full water drum, a frayed coat, a relay key, a route marker, or an unlit lamp. A resident asks the player to inspect the public ledger. The player sees the cost before accepting and can refuse without losing the ability to return. The first response creates one canonical event and one journal or archive projection; later content reads that fact through the existing owner rather than through a panel cache.

**Mechanic and system contract.** Define the input, command, event key, result, refusal, fallback, and next choice. Use existing campaign, faction, relationship, roster, expedition, shelter, archive, or ending authority as appropriate. Stateful effects use the smallest current save section with capture, restore, migration, duplicate-event handling, and a seeded replay fixture. Do not create a second reputation score, route graph, relationship network, inventory ledger, calendar, or ending state. If the premise is absent in current source or data, keep this packet unresolved and record the exact missing seam.

**Location and shelter lore.** Explain who built Cedar Lantern Classroom, what failed there, who repaired it, what custom grew from that repair, and who still pays its cost. Give the player one physical trace, one remembered phrase, one disputed interpretation, and one maintenance task. On a return visit, show the consequence before dialogue summarizes it. A quiet shelter detail should carry history: a bed rotated away from a draft, a cup reserved for visitors, a chalk line refreshed after rain, or a tool returned sharper than it was found.

**Character and faction direction.** The resident speaks plainly and notices labor before symbolism. A witness from **Cedar Lantern Tutors** uses formal language until a shortage makes the stakes concrete. A third voice may be an apprentice, courier, absent person represented by an object, or elder who remembers a different version. Give each a promise, fear, boundary, apology, refusal, and late callback. Let a minor voice receive one measurable outcome in the roster, route, archive, relationship, or ending projection.

**Story, UI, and verification.** The side quest needs an entry condition, player action, cost, consequence, refusal branch, archive fact, late-arrival variant, and missing-record variant. Prose should reveal the mechanic through ordinary work. The UI needs a compact label, expanded explanation, focus order, keyboard/controller close and back, readable long text, contrast, non-color cues, and confirmation for irreversible actions. Acceptance requires premise evidence, owner and consumer proof, focused contract or data checks, save round trip, paired deterministic replay, performance notes, and a rollback boundary. Use existing campaign, faction, relationship, roster, expedition, shelter, archive, or ending authority as appropriate. Stateful effects use the smallest current save section with capture, restore, migration, duplicate-event handling, and a seeded replay fixture. Do not create a second reputation score, route graph, relationship network, inventory ledger, calendar, or ending state. If the premise is absent in current source or data, keep this packet unresolved and record the exact missing seam.

**Location and shelter lore.** Explain who built Iron Finch Commons, what failed there, who repaired it, what custom grew from that repair, and who still pays its cost. Give the player one physical trace, one remembered phrase, one disputed interpretation, and one maintenance task. On a return visit, show the consequence before dialogue summarizes it. A quiet shelter detail should carry history: a bed rotated away from a draft, a cup reserved for visitors, a chalk line refreshed after rain, or a tool returned sharper than it was found.

**Character and faction direction.** The resident speaks plainly and notices labor before symbolism. A witness from **Iron Finch Makers** uses formal language until a shortage makes the stakes concrete. A third voice may be an apprentice, courier, absent person represented by an object, or elder who remembers a different version. Give each a promise, fear, boundary, apology, refusal, and late callback. Let a minor voice receive one measurable outcome in the roster, route, archive, relationship, or ending projection.

**Story, UI, and verification.** The side quest needs an entry condition, player action, cost, consequence, refusal branch, archive fact, late-arrival variant, and missing-record variant. Prose should reveal the mechanic through ordinary work. The UI needs a compact label, expanded explanation, focus order, keyboard/controller close and back, readable long text, contrast, non-color cues, and confirmation for irreversible actions. Acceptance requires premise evidence, owner and consumer proof, focused contract or data checks, save round trip, paired deterministic replay, performance notes, and a rollback boundary. The packet is not an implementation claim; it is ready only for a safe-slice review.

## Wave 35 supplemental receipt

The supplemental packets preserve the active twenty-field structure and broaden the playable content bank. They remain provisional until current catalog, ownership, save, replay, UI, accessibility, performance, and rollback evidence is attached.

### Wave 35 micro packet: ordinary proof in Red Willow Commons

At **Red Willow Commons**, the player can spend one quiet minute making shared care visible: a novice sets a clean cup beside the stove. The action reads the current owner, records one fact, and returns the same result after save and reload. A member of **Red Willow Makers** names the practical boundary, while a second resident supplies a memory that does not settle the dispute. The side quest offers a refusal branch, a late-arrival branch, and a missing-record branch; none creates a parallel counter. The location keeps one physical trace, the shelter keeps one custom, and the character keeps one callback. The compact UI exposes the action, cost, confirmation, focus order, and non-color feedback. Acceptance is a premise check, owner route, deterministic replay, persistence round trip, accessibility pass, and rollback note.

## Wave 35 extended depth layer

This larger tranche adds six extended packets per plan. They deepen the active twenty fields while keeping all mechanics, catalog rows, factions, locations, shelter customs, and late-game institutions provisional and owner-bound.

### Wave 35 extended depth packet 01: brokered truce calendar at Red Willow Commons

#### Extended field 01 — Premise and canon

The brokered truce calendar begins as a premise audit around Red Willow Commons. The player is asked to count the lamps before opening the door, but the proposal remains provisional until current source, JSON authority, event producer, host consumer, and ownership ledger are cited. Record the nearest existing seam, the exact absent seam, and the collision to exclude. If the premise is already represented, fold the prose into that owner and retire this packet rather than creating a duplicate.

#### Extended field 02 — Player loop

The loop has six readable beats: arrive at Red Willow Commons, inspect a practical sign, hear a resident’s account, choose a cost, perform one visible task, and return after the next weather or duty turn. The choice can preserve, delay, redirect, or refuse the request. Show the consequence before explanation. A failure gives information or a bounded recovery task unless the canonical owner defines a terminal result.

#### Extended field 03 — System contract

Route the command through the current owner for shelter culture and survivor vocations. Define command, event key, inputs, output fact, refusal, fallback, idempotency, and consumer. The packet may touch faction standing, route access, roster duty, shelter archive, relationship, expedition, or ending interpretation only through those authorities. It may not create a private truce score, route graph, calendar, inventory, reputation counter, or parallel legacy record.

#### Extended field 04 — Mechanic

Introduce one mechanic that makes maintenance and trust interact: a concession opens a safer task, a late repair changes a route window, or an honest admission reduces a future surprise. The mechanic should have a threshold, a visible cost, a reversible preparation state, and a deterministic result. The player can test the boundary in a low-risk scene before committing to the late-game version.

#### Extended field 05 — Location lore

At Cobalt Finch Classroom, describe who built the room, which flood or fire altered it, who kept the key, and why one wall remains unpainted. Give the player a physical trace, a remembered phrase, a disputed interpretation, and a maintenance action. Returning to the site should show an object moved, repaired, withheld, or shared before any dialogue summarizes the change.

#### Extended field 06 — Shelter lore

The shelter projection keeps a custom tied to the same fact: a cup reserved for a messenger, a bell rung only after consent, a cord tied around a tool, or a bench left open for the missing. The custom has a practical function and a social cost. Its archive text must name the worker who sustains it and the person who objects without reducing either voice to exposition.

#### Extended field 07 — Character voices

Write three distinct voices. A resident of Cobalt Finch Classroom notices labor and weather. A representative of Red Willow Makers speaks in careful public terms until the cost reaches a family or crew. A witness linked to Cobalt Finch Tutors remembers a different sequence. Give each a promise, fear, boundary, apology, refusal, and late callback. Let a minor voice receive a measurable roster, route, archive, or ending consequence.

#### Extended field 08 — Faction politics

The faction layer distinguishes Red Willow Makers, Cobalt Finch Tutors, Ashriver Care Circle, and South Harrow Storykeepers by resource, ritual, and risk rather than color. Red Willow Makers wants a reliable public record, Cobalt Finch Tutors protects a route custom, Ashriver Care Circle values a scarce repair skill, and South Harrow Storykeepers demands a future witness. None is automatically virtuous. Coalition progress is a projection of existing standing and event facts, with dissent and abstention preserved.

#### Extended field 09 — Story and prose

The side quest opens with an ordinary sentence: someone asks whether the lamp, map, ledger, meal, or signal can wait one more night. The player’s answer changes who performs the task and what is remembered. Use restrained prose, concrete objects, and one silence that another character interprets differently. Add calm, pressure, failure, recovery, refusal, late-arrival, and missing-record variants.

#### Extended field 10 — Late-game system

Add calm, pressure, failure, recovery, refusal, late-arrival, and missing-record variants.

#### Extended field 10 — Late-game system

The late-game form is a major faction or frontier institution that can only appear after several owner-bound facts agree. It may convene a coalition, certify a route, steward a shelter custom, or carry a legacy signal. Its powers are bounded: it can request, witness, schedule, or interpret. It cannot rewrite history, bypass save ownership, or silently convert provisional prose into canon.

#### Extended field 11 — Data and catalog

Candidate content rows for legacy signal covenant carry schema_version, snake_case ID, owner, prerequisites, references, effects, fallback text, localization key, archive policy, retirement note, and missing-data behavior. Link every row to one canonical consumer and one command. Keep Ashriver Care Room, South Harrow Meal Hall, Ashriver Care Circle, and South Harrow Storykeepers provisional until catalog aliases and reachability are proven.

#### Extended field 12 — Save and migration

Use the smallest existing save section. Capture the new fact, restore it, migrate older envelopes, tolerate an absent optional row, and make duplicate events idempotent. Define the pre-event, committed, refused, interrupted, and restored states. Do not encode prose branches in a panel cache. A rollback note must identify the event boundary and the owner responsible for undo or compensating projection.

#### Extended field 13 — Deterministic replay

Pin seed, event key, input order, and expected projection. Paired replays must agree on standing, access, route, roster, archive, or ending interpretation. Avoid wall-clock seeds, unordered iteration, hidden random choices, and locale-sensitive sorting. Include a late-arrival replay and a missing-record replay so optional content cannot alter the deterministic core unexpectedly.

#### Extended field 14 — UI and accessibility

The UI exposes a compact action label, expanded explanation, cost, consequence preview, focus order, keyboard and controller back behavior, readable long text, contrast, scaling, non-color cues, and confirmation for irreversible choices. Provide an audio or text alternative. If a record is missing, show a truthful unavailable state and preserve navigation. Archive and map panels consume projections; they do not own decisions.

#### Extended field 15 — Performance and lifecycle

Set budgets for catalog parse, query, event dispatch, archive projection, panel refresh, long text, and return visits. Load high-volume rows lazily, page them without changing order, dispose listeners on close, and avoid repeated full-catalog scans. Add one degradation path for a missing asset or provider. Note the smallest focused host smoke needed if the owner route is eventually implemented.

#### Extended field 16 — Acceptance and handoff

Acceptance requires premise evidence, owner and consumer proof, one reachable player command, save round trip, migration fixture, paired replay, accessibility review, performance notes, and a rollback boundary. The handoff names untouched shared paths and labels this as design scaffolding. The final image is practical: a repaired latch, an amended map, a divided bowl, a chalk mark, a quiet signal, or a door left open by consent.

## Wave 35 extended depth receipt

The extended layer is documentation-only. Promotion requires current premise evidence, owner and consumer proof, reachable content, deterministic persistence and replay, accessibility, performance, and rollback evidence.

## Continuation Wave 36 — Passes 384–394

This synchronized continuation keeps Fields 11–20 active. It adds new provisional factions, late-game organizations, locations, shelter customs, survivor voices, mechanics, side quests, UI/UX scaffolds, and performance or replay gates without claiming production implementation or creating parallel mutable state.

The side quest offers a refusal branch, a late-arrival branch, and a missing-record branch; none creates a parallel counter. ## Wave 36 extended depth layer

### Wave 36 extended depth packet 01: witnessed resource compact at Amber Cinder Commons

#### Extended field 01 — Premise and canon

The witnessed resource compact begins as a premise audit around Amber Cinder Commons. The player is asked to count the lamps before opening the door, but the proposal remains provisional until current source, JSON authority, event producer, host consumer, and ownership ledger are cited. Record the nearest existing seam, the exact absent seam, and the collision to exclude. If the premise is already represented, fold the prose into that owner and retire this packet rather than creating a duplicate.

#### Extended field 02 — Player loop

The loop has six readable beats: arrive at Amber Cinder Commons, inspect a practical sign, hear a resident’s account, choose a cost, perform one visible task, and return after the next weather or duty turn. The choice can preserve, delay, redirect, or refuse the request. Show the consequence before explanation. A failure gives information or a bounded recovery task unless the canonical owner defines a terminal result.

#### Extended field 03 — System contract

Route the command through the current owner for shelter culture and survivor vocations. Define command, event key, inputs, output fact, refusal, fallback, idempotency, and consumer. The packet may touch faction standing, route access, roster duty, shelter archive, relationship, expedition, or ending interpretation only through those authorities. It may not create a private truce score, route graph, calendar, inventory, reputation counter, or parallel legacy record.

#### Extended field 04 — Mechanic

Introduce one mechanic that makes maintenance and trust interact: a concession opens a safer task, a late repair changes a route window, or an honest admission reduces a future surprise. The mechanic should have a threshold, a visible cost, a reversible preparation state, and a deterministic result. The player can test the boundary in a low-risk scene before committing to the late-game version.

#### Extended field 05 — Location lore

At Mossglass Classroom, describe who built the room, which flood or fire altered it, who kept the key, and why one wall remains unpainted. Give the player a physical trace, a remembered phrase, a disputed interpretation, and a maintenance action. Returning to the site should show an object moved, repaired, withheld, or shared before any dialogue summarizes the change.

#### Extended field 06 — Shelter lore

The shelter projection keeps a custom tied to the same fact: a cup reserved for a messenger, a bell rung only after consent, a cord tied around a tool, or a bench left open for the missing. The custom has a practical function and a social cost. Its archive text must name the worker who sustains it and the person who objects without reducing either voice to exposition.

#### Extended field 07 — Character voices

Write three distinct voices. A resident of Mossglass Classroom notices labor and weather. A representative of Amber Cinder Makers speaks in careful public terms until the cost reaches a family or crew. A witness linked to Mossglass Tutors remembers a different sequence. Give each a promise, fear, boundary, apology, refusal, and late callback. Let a minor voice receive a measurable roster, route, archive, or ending consequence.

#### Extended field 08 — Faction politics

The faction layer distinguishes Amber Cinder Makers, Mossglass Tutors, Silver Rain Care Circle, and East Yarrow Storykeepers by resource, ritual, and risk rather than color. Amber Cinder Makers wants a reliable public record, Mossglass Tutors protects a route custom, Silver Rain Care Circle values a scarce repair skill, and East Yarrow Storykeepers demands a future witness. None is automatically virtuous. Coalition progress is a projection of existing standing and event facts, with dissent and abstention preserved.

#### Extended field 09 — Story and prose

The side quest opens with an ordinary sentence: someone asks whether the lamp, map, ledger, meal, or signal can wait one more night. The player’s answer changes who performs the task and what is remembered. Use restrained prose, concrete objects, and one silence that another character interprets differently. Add calm, pressure, failure, recovery, refusal, late-arrival, and missing-record variants.

#### Extended field 10 — Late-game system

The late-game form is a major faction or frontier institution that can only appear after several owner-bound facts agree. It may convene a coalition, certify a route, steward a shelter custom, or carry a legacy signal. Its powers are bounded: it can request, witness, schedule, or interpret. It cannot rewrite history, bypass save ownership, or silently convert provisional prose into canon.

#### Extended field 11 — Data and catalog

Candidate content rows for witnessed resource compact carry schema_version, snake_case ID, owner, prerequisites, references, effects, fallback text, localization key, archive policy, retirement note, and missing-data behavior. Link every row to one canonical consumer and one command. Keep Silver Rain Care Room, East Yarrow Meal Hall, Silver Rain Care Circle, and East Yarrow Storykeepers provisional until catalog aliases and reachability are proven.

#### Extended field 12 — Save and migration

Use the smallest existing save section. Capture the new fact, restore it, migrate older envelopes, tolerate an absent optional row, and make duplicate events idempotent. Define the pre-event, committed, refused, interrupted, and restored states. Do not encode prose branches in a panel cache. A rollback note must identify the event boundary and the owner responsible for undo or compensating projection.

#### Extended field 13 — Deterministic replay

Pin seed, event key, input order, and expected projection. Paired replays must agree on standing, access, route, roster, archive, or ending interpretation. Avoid wall-clock seeds, unordered iteration, hidden random choices, and locale-sensitive sorting. Include a late-arrival replay and a missing-record replay so optional content cannot alter the deterministic core unexpectedly.

#### Extended field 14 — UI and accessibility

The UI exposes a compact action label, expanded explanation, cost, consequence preview, focus order, keyboard and controller back behavior, readable long text, contrast, scaling, non-color cues, and confirmation for irreversible choices. Provide an audio or text alternative. If a record is missing, show a truthful unavailable state and preserve navigation. Archive and map panels consume projections; they do not own decisions.

#### Extended field 15 — Performance and lifecycle

Set budgets for catalog parse, query, event dispatch, archive projection, panel refresh, long text, and return visits. Load high-volume rows lazily, page them without changing order, dispose listeners on close, and avoid repeated full-catalog scans. Add one degradation path for a missing asset or provider. Note the smallest focused host smoke needed if the owner route is eventually implemented.

#### Extended field 16 — Acceptance and handoff

Acceptance requires premise evidence, owner and consumer proof, one reachable player command, save round trip, migration fixture, paired replay, accessibility review, performance notes, and a rollback boundary. The handoff names untouched shared paths and labels this as design scaffolding. ### Supplemental packet 01: shelter culture and survivor vocations — Blue Orchard Classroom action 1

The scene opens at **Blue Orchard Classroom**, where the practical detail is more urgent than the ceremonial language: a damp ledger, a half-full water drum, a frayed coat, a relay key, a route marker, or an unlit lamp. A resident asks the player to inspect the public ledger. The player sees the cost before accepting and can refuse without losing the ability to return. The first response creates one canonical event and one journal or archive projection; later content reads that fact through the existing owner rather than through a panel cache.

Give the player one physical trace, one remembered phrase, one disputed interpretation, and one maintenance task. On a return visit, show the consequence before dialogue summarizes it. A quiet shelter detail should carry history: a bed rotated away from a draft, a cup reserved for visitors, a chalk line refreshed after rain, or a tool returned sharper than it was found.

A witness from **Blue Orchard Tutors** uses formal language until a shortage makes the stakes concrete. A third voice may be an apprentice, courier, absent person represented by an object, or elder who remembers a different version. Give each a promise, fear, boundary, apology, refusal, and late callback. Let a minor voice receive one measurable outcome in the roster, route, archive, relationship, or ending projection.

**Location and shelter lore.** Explain who built Marrowlight Commons, what failed there, who repaired it, what custom grew from that repair, and who still pays its cost. Give the player one physical trace, one remembered phrase, one disputed interpretation, and one maintenance task. On a return visit, show the consequence before dialogue summarizes it. A quiet shelter detail should carry history: a bed rotated away from a draft, a cup reserved for visitors, a chalk line refreshed after rain, or a tool returned sharper than it was found.

**Character and faction direction.** The resident speaks plainly and notices labor before symbolism. A witness from **Marrowlight Makers** uses formal language until a shortage makes the stakes concrete. A third voice may be an apprentice, courier, absent person represented by an object, or elder who remembers a different version. Give each a promise, fear, boundary, apology, refusal, and late callback. Let a minor voice receive one measurable outcome in the roster, route, archive, relationship, or ending projection.

**Story, UI, and verification.** The side quest needs an entry condition, player action, cost, consequence, refusal branch, archive fact, late-arrival variant, and missing-record variant. Prose should reveal the mechanic through ordinary work. The UI needs a compact label, expanded explanation, focus order, keyboard/controller close and back, readable long text, contrast, non-color cues, and confirmation for irreversible actions. Acceptance requires premise evidence, owner and consumer proof, focused contract or data checks, save round trip, paired deterministic replay, performance notes, and a rollback boundary. The packet is not an implementation claim; it is ready only for a safe-slice review.


## Wave 37 supplemental receipt

The supplemental packets preserve the active twenty-field structure and broaden the playable content bank. They remain provisional until current catalog, ownership, save, replay, UI, accessibility, performance, and rollback evidence is attached.

## Wave 37 extended depth layer

This larger tranche adds six extended packets per plan. They deepen the active twenty fields while keeping all mechanics, catalog rows, factions, locations, shelter customs, and late-game institutions provisional and owner-bound.

### Wave 37 extended depth packet 01: public witness compact at Marrowlight Commons

#### Extended field 01 — Premise and canon

The public witness compact begins as a premise audit around Marrowlight Commons. The player is asked to count the lamps before opening the door, but the proposal remains provisional until current source, JSON authority, event producer, host consumer, and ownership ledger are cited. Record the nearest existing seam, the exact absent seam, and the collision to exclude. If the premise is already represented, fold the prose into that owner and retire this packet rather than creating a duplicate.

#### Extended field 02 — Player loop

The loop has six readable beats: arrive at Marrowlight Commons, inspect a practical sign, hear a resident’s account, choose a cost, perform one visible task, and return after the next weather or duty turn. The choice can preserve, delay, redirect, or refuse the request. Show the consequence before explanation. A failure gives information or a bounded recovery task unless the canonical owner defines a terminal result.

#### Extended field 03 — System contract

Route the command through the current owner for shelter culture and survivor vocations. Define command, event key, inputs, output fact, refusal, fallback, idempotency, and consumer. The packet may touch faction standing, route access, roster duty, shelter archive, relationship, expedition, or ending interpretation only through those authorities. It may not create a private truce score, route graph, calendar, inventory, reputation counter, or parallel legacy record.

#### Extended field 04 — Mechanic

Introduce one mechanic that makes maintenance and trust interact: a concession opens a safer task, a late repair changes a route window, or an honest admission reduces a future surprise. The mechanic should have a threshold, a visible cost, a reversible preparation state, and a deterministic result. The player can test the boundary in a low-risk scene before committing to the late-game version.

#### Extended field 05 — Location lore

At Blue Orchard Classroom, describe who built the room, which flood or fire altered it, who kept the key, and why one wall remains unpainted. Give the player a physical trace, a remembered phrase, a disputed interpretation, and a maintenance action. Returning to the site should show an object moved, repaired, withheld, or shared before any dialogue summarizes the change.

#### Extended field 06 — Shelter lore

The shelter projection keeps a custom tied to the same fact: a cup reserved for a messenger, a bell rung only after consent, a cord tied around a tool, or a bench left open for the missing. The custom has a practical function and a social cost. Its archive text must name the worker who sustains it and the person who objects without reducing either voice to exposition.

#### Extended field 07 — Character voices

Write three distinct voices. A resident of Blue Orchard Classroom notices labor and weather. A representative of Marrowlight Makers speaks in careful public terms until the cost reaches a family or crew. A witness linked to Blue Orchard Tutors remembers a different sequence. Give each a promise, fear, boundary, apology, refusal, and late callback. Let a minor voice receive a measurable roster, route, archive, or ending consequence.

#### Extended field 08 — Faction politics

The faction layer distinguishes Marrowlight Makers, Blue Orchard Tutors, Copper Haze Care Circle, and East Sable Storykeepers by resource, ritual, and risk rather than color. Marrowlight Makers wants a reliable public record, Blue Orchard Tutors protects a route custom, Copper Haze Care Circle values a scarce repair skill, and East Sable Storykeepers demands a future witness. None is automatically virtuous. Coalition progress is a projection of existing standing and event facts, with dissent and abstention preserved.

#### Extended field 09 — Story and prose

The side quest opens with an ordinary sentence: someone asks whether the lamp, map, ledger, meal, or signal can wait one more night. The player’s answer changes who performs the task and what is remembered. Use restrained prose, concrete objects, and one silence that another character interprets differently. Add calm, pressure, failure, recovery, refusal, late-arrival, and missing-record variants.

#### Extended field 10 — Late-game system

The late-game form is a major faction or frontier institution that can only appear after several owner-bound facts agree. It may convene a coalition, certify a route, steward a shelter custom, or carry a legacy signal. Its powers are bounded: it can request, witness, schedule, or interpret. It cannot rewrite history, bypass save ownership, or silently convert provisional prose into canon.

#### Extended field 11 — Data and catalog

Candidate content rows for public witness compact carry schema_version, snake_case ID, owner, prerequisites, references, effects, fallback text, localization key, archive policy, retirement note, and missing-data behavior. Link every row to one canonical consumer and one command. Keep Copper Haze Care Room, East Sable Meal Hall, Copper Haze Care Circle, and East Sable Storykeepers provisional until catalog aliases and reachability are proven.

#### Extended field 12 — Save and migration

Use the smallest existing save section. Capture the new fact, restore it, migrate older envelopes, tolerate an absent optional row, and make duplicate events idempotent. Define the pre-event, committed, refused, interrupted, and restored states. Do not encode prose branches in a panel cache. A rollback note must identify the event boundary and the owner responsible for undo or compensating projection.

#### Extended field 13 — Deterministic replay

Pin seed, event key, input order, and expected projection. Paired replays must agree on standing, access, route, roster, archive, or ending interpretation. Avoid wall-clock seeds, unordered iteration, hidden random choices, and locale-sensitive sorting. Include a late-arrival replay and a missing-record replay so optional content cannot alter the deterministic core unexpectedly.

#### Extended field 14 — UI and accessibility

The UI exposes a compact action label, expanded explanation, cost, consequence preview, focus order, keyboard and controller back behavior, readable long text, contrast, scaling, non-color cues, and confirmation for irreversible choices. Provide an audio or text alternative. If a record is missing, show a truthful unavailable state and preserve navigation. Archive and map panels consume projections; they do not own decisions.

#### Extended field 15 — Performance and lifecycle

Set budgets for catalog parse, query, event dispatch, archive projection, panel refresh, long text, and return visits. Load high-volume rows lazily, page them without changing order, dispose listeners on close, and avoid repeated full-catalog scans. Add one degradation path for a missing asset or provider. Note the smallest focused host smoke needed if the owner route is eventually implemented.

#### Extended field 16 — Acceptance and handoff

Acceptance requires premise evidence, owner and consumer proof, one reachable player command, save round trip, migration fixture, paired replay, accessibility review, performance notes, and a rollback boundary. The handoff names untouched shared paths and labels this as design scaffolding. The final image is practical: a repaired latch, an amended map, a divided bowl, a chalk mark, a quiet signal, or a door left open by consent.

## Wave 38 supplemental receipt

The supplemental packets preserve the active twenty-field structure and broaden the playable content bank. They remain provisional until current catalog, ownership, save, replay, UI, accessibility, performance, and rollback evidence is attached.

## Wave 38 extended depth layer

This larger tranche adds six extended packets per plan. They deepen the active twenty fields while keeping all mechanics, catalog rows, factions, locations, shelter customs, and late-game institutions provisional and owner-bound.

### Wave 38 extended depth packet 01: shared burden compact at Hearthblue Commons

#### Extended field 01 — Premise and canon

The shared burden compact begins as a premise audit around Hearthblue Commons. The player is asked to count the lamps before opening the door, but the proposal remains provisional until current source, JSON authority, event producer, host consumer, and ownership ledger are cited. Record the nearest existing seam, the exact absent seam, and the collision to exclude. If the premise is already represented, fold the prose into that owner and retire this packet rather than creating a duplicate.

#### Extended field 02 — Player loop

The loop has six readable beats: arrive at Hearthblue Commons, inspect a practical sign, hear a resident’s account, choose a cost, perform one visible task, and return after the next weather or duty turn. The choice can preserve, delay, redirect, or refuse the request. Show the consequence before explanation. A failure gives information or a bounded recovery task unless the canonical owner defines a terminal result.

#### Extended field 03 — System contract

Route the command through the current owner for shelter culture and survivor vocations. Define command, event key, inputs, output fact, refusal, fallback, idempotency, and consumer. The packet may touch faction standing, route access, roster duty, shelter archive, relationship, expedition, or ending interpretation only through those authorities. It may not create a private truce score, route graph, calendar, inventory, reputation counter, or parallel legacy record.

#### Extended field 04 — Mechanic

Introduce one mechanic that makes maintenance and trust interact: a concession opens a safer task, a late repair changes a route window, or an honest admission reduces a future surprise. The mechanic should have a threshold, a visible cost, a reversible preparation state, and a deterministic result. The player can test the boundary in a low-risk scene before committing to the late-game version.

#### Extended field 05 — Location lore

At Red Vale Classroom, describe who built the room, which flood or fire altered it, who kept the key, and why one wall remains unpainted. Give the player a physical trace, a remembered phrase, a disputed interpretation, and a maintenance action. Returning to the site should show an object moved, repaired, withheld, or shared before any dialogue summarizes the change.

#### Extended field 06 — Shelter lore

The shelter projection keeps a custom tied to the same fact: a cup reserved for a messenger, a bell rung only after consent, a cord tied around a tool, or a bench left open for the missing. The custom has a practical function and a social cost. Its archive text must name the worker who sustains it and the person who objects without reducing either voice to exposition.

#### Extended field 07 — Character voices

Write three distinct voices. A resident of Red Vale Classroom notices labor and weather. A representative of Hearthblue Makers speaks in careful public terms until the cost reaches a family or crew. A witness linked to Red Vale Tutors remembers a different sequence. Give each a promise, fear, boundary, apology, refusal, and late callback. Let a minor voice receive a measurable roster, route, archive, or ending consequence.

#### Extended field 08 — Faction politics

The faction layer distinguishes Hearthblue Makers, Red Vale Tutors, Lumen Fog Care Circle, and West Bracken Storykeepers by resource, ritual, and risk rather than color. Hearthblue Makers wants a reliable public record, Red Vale Tutors protects a route custom, Lumen Fog Care Circle values a scarce repair skill, and West Bracken Storykeepers demands a future witness. None is automatically virtuous. Coalition progress is a projection of existing standing and event facts, with dissent and abstention preserved.

#### Extended field 09 — Story and prose

The side quest opens with an ordinary sentence: someone asks whether the lamp, map, ledger, meal, or signal can wait one more night. The player’s answer changes who performs the task and what is remembered. Use restrained prose, concrete objects, and one silence that another character interprets differently. Add calm, pressure, failure, recovery, refusal, late-arrival, and missing-record variants.

#### Extended field 10 — Late-game system

The late-game form is a major faction or frontier institution that can only appear after several owner-bound facts agree. It may convene a coalition, certify a route, steward a shelter custom, or carry a legacy signal. Its powers are bounded: it can request, witness, schedule, or interpret. It cannot rewrite history, bypass save ownership, or silently convert provisional prose into canon.

#### Extended field 11 — Data and catalog

Candidate content rows for shared burden compact carry schema_version, snake_case ID, owner, prerequisites, references, effects, fallback text, localization key, archive policy, retirement note, and missing-data behavior. Link every row to one canonical consumer and one command. Keep Lumen Fog Care Room, West Bracken Meal Hall, Lumen Fog Care Circle, and West Bracken Storykeepers provisional until catalog aliases and reachability are proven.

#### Extended field 12 — Save and migration

Use the smallest existing save section. Capture the new fact, restore it, migrate older envelopes, tolerate an absent optional row, and make duplicate events idempotent. Define the pre-event, committed, refused, interrupted, and restored states. Do not encode prose branches in a panel cache. A rollback note must identify the event boundary and the owner responsible for undo or compensating projection.

#### Extended field 13 — Deterministic replay

Pin seed, event key, input order, and expected projection. Paired replays must agree on standing, access, route, roster, archive, or ending interpretation. Avoid wall-clock seeds, unordered iteration, hidden random choices, and locale-sensitive sorting. Include a late-arrival replay and a missing-record replay so optional content cannot alter the deterministic core unexpectedly.

#### Extended field 14 — UI and accessibility

The UI exposes a compact action label, expanded explanation, cost, consequence preview, focus order, keyboard and controller back behavior, readable long text, contrast, scaling, non-color cues, and confirmation for irreversible choices. Provide an audio or text alternative. If a record is missing, show a truthful unavailable state and preserve navigation. Archive and map panels consume projections; they do not own decisions.

#### Extended field 15 — Performance and lifecycle

Set budgets for catalog parse, query, event dispatch, archive projection, panel refresh, long text, and return visits. Load high-volume rows lazily, page them without changing order, dispose listeners on close, and avoid repeated full-catalog scans. Add one degradation path for a missing asset or provider. Note the smallest focused host smoke needed if the owner route is eventually implemented.

#### Extended field 16 — Acceptance and handoff

Acceptance requires premise evidence, owner and consumer proof, one reachable player command, save round trip, migration fixture, paired replay, accessibility review, performance notes, and a rollback boundary. The handoff names untouched shared paths and labels this as design scaffolding. The final image is practical: a repaired latch, an amended map, a divided bowl, a chalk mark, a quiet signal, or a door left open by consent.

## Wave 38 capsule layer

### Wave 38 capsule 01: weather-window arbitration at Hearthblue Commons

**Opening and choice.** At **Hearthblue Commons**, the player finds a practical problem that cannot be solved by rhetoric alone: a weather window is closing, a shared tool has two claimants, a missing person may be returning, a night signal is being misread, an apprentice is ready before the shelter is ready, a water ration has been counted twice, a quiet route carries an old debt, or a legacy object must be placed in another person’s hands. The player inspects the evidence, asks for consent, compares accounts, chooses a cost, defers, or leaves. The cost appears before commitment and a refusal keeps a safe return path.

**Authority and mechanic.** Route the action through the current owner for shelter culture and survivor vocations. Define one command, one event key, one resulting fact, one refusal result, one fallback, and one idempotency rule. A derived readiness view may combine existing standing, relationship, route, roster, shelter, archive, expedition, or ending facts, but it cannot become a second ledger or clock. The mechanic should make an ordinary task consequential: rescheduling a crossing changes who carries a tool, recording a signal changes which watch is asked to stand, or accepting a handover changes who is invited to the next meeting. The player can test the boundary in a low-risk version first.

**Place and shelter lore.** At **Red Vale Classroom**, describe the builder, the repair that saved the room, the person who still pays for that repair, and the mark that remains unexplained. At **Lumen Fog Care Room**, place a contrasting trace: a patched hinge, a dry shelf, an erased route line, a bell rope, a teaching slate, or a bowl set aside. At **West Bracken Meal Hall**, let a shelter custom make the history useful: a lamp is moved only after consent, a tool is returned sharpened, a guest cup is washed before dawn, or a route name is spoken once and then left unclaimed. Returning to the location shows a changed object before exposition.

**Characters and factions.** A resident speaks in concrete duties and notices who will carry the burden. A representative of **Hearthblue Makers** uses public language and wants an auditable result. A voice from **Red Vale Tutors** protects a custom that looks inefficient until its history is heard. **Lumen Fog Care Circle** values a scarce skill, while **West Bracken Storykeepers** asks who will witness the consequence after the player leaves. Give each voice a promise, fear, boundary, apology, refusal, and callback. The late-game factional version may convene a coalition, certify a passage, steward a shelter custom, or preserve a memory, but it may request and witness only through existing authorities.

**Story and prose.** The scene opens with one quiet sentence about work: “The rope is dry enough for one more crossing,” “The cup was left where the missing person could find it,” or “The bell was rung before anyone agreed.” The player’s response changes who performs the task, what the journal remembers, and which later character feels entitled to speak. Add calm, pressure, failure, recovery, refusal, late-arrival, and missing-record variants. Use concrete objects, short silences, and a callback that makes the earlier mechanic visible without turning the packet into a lore lecture.

**Data and content volume.** Candidate rows carry schema_version, snake_case ID, owner, prerequisites, references, effects, fallback text, localization key, archive policy, retirement note, and missing-data behavior. Create arrival, inspection, task, hazard, rest, departure, return, calm, pressure, failure, recovery, refusal, and late-arrival variants. Define one command, one event key, one resulting fact, one refusal result, one fallback, and one idempotency rule. A derived readiness view may combine existing standing, relationship, route, roster, shelter, archive, expedition, or ending facts, but it cannot become a second ledger or clock. The mechanic should make an ordinary task consequential: rescheduling a crossing changes who carries a tool, recording a signal changes which watch is asked to stand, or accepting a handover changes who is invited to the next meeting. The player can test the boundary in a low-risk version first.

**Place and shelter lore.** At **Red Vale Classroom**, describe the builder, the repair that saved the room, the person who still pays for that repair, and the mark that remains unexplained. At **Lumen Fog Care Room**, place a contrasting trace: a patched hinge, a dry shelf, an erased route line, a bell rope, a teaching slate, or a bowl set aside. At **West Bracken Meal Hall**, let a shelter custom make the history useful: a lamp is moved only after consent, a tool is returned sharpened, a guest cup is washed before dawn, or a route name is spoken once and then left unclaimed. Returning to the location shows a changed object before exposition.

**Characters and factions.** A resident speaks in concrete duties and notices who will carry the burden. A representative of **Hearthblue Makers** uses public language and wants an auditable result. A voice from **Red Vale Tutors** protects a custom that looks inefficient until its history is heard. **Lumen Fog Care Circle** values a scarce skill, while **West Bracken Storykeepers** asks who will witness the consequence after the player leaves. Give each voice a promise, fear, boundary, apology, refusal, and callback. The late-game factional version may convene a coalition, certify a passage, steward a shelter custom, or preserve a memory, but it may request and witness only through existing authorities.

**Story and prose.** The scene opens with one quiet sentence about work: “The rope is dry enough for one more crossing,” “The cup was left where the missing person could find it,” or “The bell was rung before anyone agreed.” The player’s response changes who performs the task, what the journal remembers, and which later character feels entitled to speak. Add calm, pressure, failure, recovery, refusal, late-arrival, and missing-record variants. Use concrete objects, short silences, and a callback that makes the earlier mechanic visible without turning the packet into a lore lecture.

**Data and content volume.** Candidate rows carry schema_version, snake_case ID, owner, prerequisites, references, effects, fallback text, localization key, archive policy, retirement note, and missing-data behavior. Create arrival, inspection, task, hazard, rest, departure, return, calm, pressure, failure, recovery, refusal, and late-arrival variants. Keep the names of **Hearthblue Makers**, **Red Vale Tutors**, **Lumen Fog Care Circle**, and **West Bracken Storykeepers** provisional until catalog aliases and reachability are proven. A missing optional row should collapse to a truthful unavailable state rather than alter the deterministic core.

**Persistence and replay.** Capture the smallest new fact through the existing save section. Define pre-action, committed, refused, interrupted, restored, migrated, and duplicate-event states. Pin the campaign seed, event key, input order, and expected projection. Paired replays must agree on standing, access, route, roster, archive, or ending interpretation, including the late-arrival and missing-record cases. Do not use wall-clock seeds, unordered iteration, locale-sensitive sorting, or hidden randomness in prose.

**UI, accessibility, and lifecycle.** Expose a compact action label, expanded explanation, cost, consequence preview, focus order, keyboard/controller close and back, readable long text, contrast, scaling, non-color cues, confirmation for irreversible actions, and text or audio alternatives. Panels consume owner projections and dispose listeners on close. High-volume rows load lazily and page without changing order. Set budgets for parse, query, dispatch, archive projection, refresh, and return visits; document the missing-provider path and the smallest eventual host smoke.

**Acceptance and handoff.** Accept the capsule only with premise evidence, owner and consumer proof, one reachable command, save round trip, migration fixture, paired replay, accessibility review, performance notes, and rollback. The handoff records untouched shared paths and labels the content as design scaffolding. The final image is small and physical: a cord retied, a cup passed over, a map corrected, a signal answered, a tool returned sharper, a meal divided, or a door left open because someone was asked first.

## Wave 39 supplemental receipt
