## Wave 39 extended depth layer

This larger tranche adds six extended packets per plan. They deepen the active twenty fields while keeping all mechanics, catalog rows, factions, locations, shelter customs, and late-game institutions provisional and owner-bound.

### Wave 39 extended depth packet 01: public repair compact at Sunken Juniper Commons

#### Extended field 01 — Premise and canon

The public repair compact begins as a premise audit around Sunken Juniper Commons. The player is asked to count the lamps before opening the door, but the proposal remains provisional until current source, JSON authority, event producer, host consumer, and ownership ledger are cited. Record the nearest existing seam, the exact absent seam, and the collision to exclude. If the premise is already represented, fold the prose into that owner and retire this packet rather than creating a duplicate.

#### Extended field 02 — Player loop

The loop has six readable beats: arrive at Sunken Juniper Commons, inspect a practical sign, hear a resident’s account, choose a cost, perform one visible task, and return after the next weather or duty turn. The choice can preserve, delay, redirect, or refuse the request. Show the consequence before explanation. A failure gives information or a bounded recovery task unless the canonical owner defines a terminal result.

#### Extended field 03 — System contract

Route the command through the current owner for shelter culture and survivor vocations. Define command, event key, inputs, output fact, refusal, fallback, idempotency, and consumer. The packet may touch faction standing, route access, roster duty, shelter archive, relationship, expedition, or ending interpretation only through those authorities. It may not create a private truce score, route graph, calendar, inventory, reputation counter, or parallel legacy record.

#### Extended field 04 — Mechanic

Introduce one mechanic that makes maintenance and trust interact: a concession opens a safer task, a late repair changes a route window, or an honest admission reduces a future surprise. The mechanic should have a threshold, a visible cost, a reversible preparation state, and a deterministic result. The player can test the boundary in a low-risk scene before committing to the late-game version.

#### Extended field 05 — Location lore

At Pale Orchard Classroom, describe who built the room, which flood or fire altered it, who kept the key, and why one wall remains unpainted. Give the player a physical trace, a remembered phrase, a disputed interpretation, and a maintenance action. Returning to the site should show an object moved, repaired, withheld, or shared before any dialogue summarizes the change.

#### Extended field 06 — Shelter lore

The shelter projection keeps a custom tied to the same fact: a cup reserved for a messenger, a bell rung only after consent, a cord tied around a tool, or a bench left open for the missing. The custom has a practical function and a social cost. Its archive text must name the worker who sustains it and the person who objects without reducing either voice to exposition.

#### Extended field 07 — Character voices

Write three distinct voices. A resident of Pale Orchard Classroom notices labor and weather. A representative of Sunken Juniper Makers speaks in careful public terms until the cost reaches a family or crew. A witness linked to Pale Orchard Tutors remembers a different sequence. Give each a promise, fear, boundary, apology, refusal, and late callback. Let a minor voice receive a measurable roster, route, archive, or ending consequence.

#### Extended field 08 — Faction politics

The faction layer distinguishes Sunken Juniper Makers, Pale Orchard Tutors, Ember Mist Care Circle, and South Kestrel Storykeepers by resource, ritual, and risk rather than color. Sunken Juniper Makers wants a reliable public record, Pale Orchard Tutors protects a route custom, Ember Mist Care Circle values a scarce repair skill, and South Kestrel Storykeepers demands a future witness. None is automatically virtuous. Coalition progress is a projection of existing standing and event facts, with dissent and abstention preserved.

#### Extended field 09 — Story and prose

The side quest opens with an ordinary sentence: someone asks whether the lamp, map, ledger, meal, or signal can wait one more night. The player’s answer changes who performs the task and what is remembered. Use restrained prose, concrete objects, and one silence that another character interprets differently. Add calm, pressure, failure, recovery, refusal, late-arrival, and missing-record variants.

#### Extended field 10 — Late-game system

The late-game form is a major faction or frontier institution that can only appear after several owner-bound facts agree. It may convene a coalition, certify a route, steward a shelter custom, or carry a legacy signal. Its powers are bounded: it can request, witness, schedule, or interpret. It cannot rewrite history, bypass save ownership, or silently convert provisional prose into canon.

#### Extended field 11 — Data and catalog

Candidate content rows for public repair compact carry schema_version, snake_case ID, owner, prerequisites, references, effects, fallback text, localization key, archive policy, retirement note, and missing-data behavior. Link every row to one canonical consumer and one command. Keep Ember Mist Care Room, South Kestrel Meal Hall, Ember Mist Care Circle, and South Kestrel Storykeepers provisional until catalog aliases and reachability are proven.

#### Extended field 12 — Save and migration

Use the smallest existing save section. Capture the new fact, restore it, migrate older envelopes, tolerate an absent optional row, and make duplicate events idempotent. Define the pre-event, committed, refused, interrupted, and restored states. Do not encode prose branches in a panel cache. A rollback note must identify the event boundary and the owner responsible for undo or compensating projection.

#### Extended field 13 — Deterministic replay

Pin seed, event key, input order, and expected projection. Paired replays must agree on standing, access, route, roster, archive, or ending interpretation. Avoid wall-clock seeds, unordered iteration, hidden random choices, and locale-sensitive sorting. Include a late-arrival replay and a missing-record replay so optional content cannot alter the deterministic core unexpectedly.

#### Extended field 14 — UI and accessibility

The UI exposes a compact action label, expanded explanation, cost, consequence preview, focus order, keyboard and controller back behavior, readable long text, contrast, scaling, non-color cues, and confirmation for irreversible choices. Provide an audio or text alternative. If a record is missing, show a truthful unavailable state and preserve navigation. Archive and map panels consume projections; they do not own decisions.

#### Extended field 15 — Performance and lifecycle

Set budgets for catalog parse, query, event dispatch, archive projection, panel refresh, long text, and return visits. Load high-volume rows lazily, page them without changing order, dispose listeners on close, and avoid repeated full-catalog scans. Add one degradation path for a missing asset or provider. Note the smallest focused host smoke needed if the owner route is eventually implemented.

#### Extended field 16 — Acceptance and handoff

Acceptance requires premise evidence, owner and consumer proof, one reachable player command, save round trip, migration fixture, paired replay, accessibility review, performance notes, and a rollback boundary. The handoff names untouched shared paths and labels this as design scaffolding. The final image is practical: a repaired latch, an amended map, a divided bowl, a chalk mark, a quiet signal, or a door left open by consent.

### Wave 39 capsule 01: ashfall timing arbitration at Sunken Juniper Commons

**Opening and choice.** At **Sunken Juniper Commons**, the player finds a practical problem that cannot be solved by rhetoric alone: a weather window is closing, a shared tool has two claimants, a missing person may be returning, a night signal is being misread, an apprentice is ready before the shelter is ready, a water ration has been counted twice, a quiet route carries an old debt, or a legacy object must be placed in another person’s hands. The player inspects the evidence, asks for consent, compares accounts, chooses a cost, defers, or leaves. The cost appears before commitment and a refusal keeps a safe return path.

**Authority and mechanic.** Route the action through the current owner for shelter culture and survivor vocations. Define one command, one event key, one resulting fact, one refusal result, one fallback, and one idempotency rule. A derived readiness view may combine existing standing, relationship, route, roster, shelter, archive, expedition, or ending facts, but it cannot become a second ledger or clock. The mechanic should make an ordinary task consequential: rescheduling a crossing changes who carries a tool, recording a signal changes which watch is asked to stand, or accepting a handover changes who is invited to the next meeting. The player can test the boundary in a low-risk version first.

**Place and shelter lore.** At **Pale Orchard Classroom**, describe the builder, the repair that saved the room, the person who still pays for that repair, and the mark that remains unexplained. At **Ember Mist Care Room**, place a contrasting trace: a patched hinge, a dry shelf, an erased route line, a bell rope, a teaching slate, or a bowl set aside. At **South Kestrel Meal Hall**, let a shelter custom make the history useful: a lamp is moved only after consent, a tool is returned sharpened, a guest cup is washed before dawn, or a route name is spoken once and then left unclaimed. Returning to the location shows a changed object before exposition.

**Characters and factions.** A resident speaks in concrete duties and notices who will carry the burden. A representative of **Sunken Juniper Makers** uses public language and wants an auditable result. A voice from **Pale Orchard Tutors** protects a custom that looks inefficient until its history is heard. **Ember Mist Care Circle** values a scarce skill, while **South Kestrel Storykeepers** asks who will witness the consequence after the player leaves. Give each voice a promise, fear, boundary, apology, refusal, and callback. The late-game factional version may convene a coalition, certify a passage, steward a shelter custom, or preserve a memory, but it may request and witness only through existing authorities.

**Story and prose.** The scene opens with one quiet sentence about work: “The rope is dry enough for one more crossing,” “The cup was left where the missing person could find it,” or “The bell was rung before anyone agreed.” The player’s response changes who performs the task, what the journal remembers, and which later character feels entitled to speak. Add calm, pressure, failure, recovery, refusal, late-arrival, and missing-record variants. Use concrete objects, short silences, and a callback that makes the earlier mechanic visible without turning the packet into a lore lecture.

**Data and content volume.** Candidate rows carry schema_version, snake_case ID, owner, prerequisites, references, effects, fallback text, localization key, archive policy, retirement note, and missing-data behavior. Create arrival, inspection, task, hazard, rest, departure, return, calm, pressure, failure, recovery, refusal, and late-arrival variants. Keep the names of **Sunken Juniper Makers**, **Pale Orchard Tutors**, **Ember Mist Care Circle**, and **South Kestrel Storykeepers** provisional until catalog aliases and reachability are proven. A missing optional row should collapse to a truthful unavailable state rather than alter the deterministic core.

**Persistence and replay.** Capture the smallest new fact through the existing save section. Define pre-action, committed, refused, interrupted, restored, migrated, and duplicate-event states. Pin the campaign seed, event key, input order, and expected projection. Paired replays must agree on standing, access, route, roster, archive, or ending interpretation, including the late-arrival and missing-record cases. Do not use wall-clock seeds, unordered iteration, locale-sensitive sorting, or hidden randomness in prose.

**UI, accessibility, and lifecycle.** Expose a compact action label, expanded explanation, cost, consequence preview, focus order, keyboard/controller close and back, readable long text, contrast, scaling, non-color cues, confirmation for irreversible actions, and text or audio alternatives. Panels consume owner projections and dispose listeners on close. High-volume rows load lazily and page without changing order. Set budgets for parse, query, dispatch, archive projection, refresh, and return visits; document the missing-provider path and the smallest eventual host smoke.

**Acceptance and handoff.** Accept the capsule only with premise evidence, owner and consumer proof, one reachable command, save round trip, migration fixture, paired replay, accessibility review, performance notes, and rollback. The handoff records untouched shared paths and labels the content as design scaffolding. The final image is small and physical: a cord retied, a cup passed over, a map corrected, a signal answered, a tool returned sharper, a meal divided, or a door left open because someone was asked first.

## Wave 40 supplemental receipt

The supplemental packets preserve the active twenty-field structure and broaden the playable content bank. They remain provisional until current catalog, ownership, save, replay, UI, accessibility, performance, and rollback evidence is attached.

## Wave 40 extended depth layer

This larger tranche adds six extended packets per plan. They deepen the active twenty fields while keeping all mechanics, catalog rows, factions, locations, shelter customs, and late-game institutions provisional and owner-bound.

### Wave 40 extended depth packet 01: patient repair compact at Cinderwillow Commons

#### Extended field 01 — Premise and canon

The patient repair compact begins as a premise audit around Cinderwillow Commons. The player is asked to count the lamps before opening the door, but the proposal remains provisional until current source, JSON authority, event producer, host consumer, and ownership ledger are cited. Record the nearest existing seam, the exact absent seam, and the collision to exclude. If the premise is already represented, fold the prose into that owner and retire this packet rather than creating a duplicate.

#### Extended field 02 — Player loop

The loop has six readable beats: arrive at Cinderwillow Commons, inspect a practical sign, hear a resident’s account, choose a cost, perform one visible task, and return after the next weather or duty turn. The choice can preserve, delay, redirect, or refuse the request. Show the consequence before explanation. A failure gives information or a bounded recovery task unless the canonical owner defines a terminal result.

#### Extended field 03 — System contract

Route the command through the current owner for shelter culture and survivor vocations. Define command, event key, inputs, output fact, refusal, fallback, idempotency, and consumer. The packet may touch faction standing, route access, roster duty, shelter archive, relationship, expedition, or ending interpretation only through those authorities. It may not create a private truce score, route graph, calendar, inventory, reputation counter, or parallel legacy record.

#### Extended field 04 — Mechanic

Introduce one mechanic that makes maintenance and trust interact: a concession opens a safer task, a late repair changes a route window, or an honest admission reduces a future surprise. The mechanic should have a threshold, a visible cost, a reversible preparation state, and a deterministic result. The player can test the boundary in a low-risk scene before committing to the late-game version.

#### Extended field 05 — Location lore

At White River Classroom, describe who built the room, which flood or fire altered it, who kept the key, and why one wall remains unpainted. Give the player a physical trace, a remembered phrase, a disputed interpretation, and a maintenance action. Returning to the site should show an object moved, repaired, withheld, or shared before any dialogue summarizes the change.

#### Extended field 06 — Shelter lore

The shelter projection keeps a custom tied to the same fact: a cup reserved for a messenger, a bell rung only after consent, a cord tied around a tool, or a bench left open for the missing. The custom has a practical function and a social cost. Its archive text must name the worker who sustains it and the person who objects without reducing either voice to exposition.

#### Extended field 07 — Character voices

Write three distinct voices. A resident of White River Classroom notices labor and weather. A representative of Cinderwillow Makers speaks in careful public terms until the cost reaches a family or crew. A witness linked to White River Tutors remembers a different sequence. Give each a promise, fear, boundary, apology, refusal, and late callback. Let a minor voice receive a measurable roster, route, archive, or ending consequence.

#### Extended field 08 — Faction politics

The faction layer distinguishes Cinderwillow Makers, White River Tutors, Indigo Ash Care Circle, and North Lark Storykeepers by resource, ritual, and risk rather than color. Cinderwillow Makers wants a reliable public record, White River Tutors protects a route custom, Indigo Ash Care Circle values a scarce repair skill, and North Lark Storykeepers demands a future witness. None is automatically virtuous. Coalition progress is a projection of existing standing and event facts, with dissent and abstention preserved.

#### Extended field 09 — Story and prose

The side quest opens with an ordinary sentence: someone asks whether the lamp, map, ledger, meal, or signal can wait one more night. The player’s answer changes who performs the task and what is remembered. Use restrained prose, concrete objects, and one silence that another character interprets differently. Add calm, pressure, failure, recovery, refusal, late-arrival, and missing-record variants.

#### Extended field 10 — Late-game system

The late-game form is a major faction or frontier institution that can only appear after several owner-bound facts agree. It may convene a coalition, certify a route, steward a shelter custom, or carry a legacy signal. Its powers are bounded: it can request, witness, schedule, or interpret. It cannot rewrite history, bypass save ownership, or silently convert provisional prose into canon.

#### Extended field 11 — Data and catalog

Candidate content rows for patient repair compact carry schema_version, snake_case ID, owner, prerequisites, references, effects, fallback text, localization key, archive policy, retirement note, and missing-data behavior. Link every row to one canonical consumer and one command. Keep Indigo Ash Care Room, North Lark Meal Hall, Indigo Ash Care Circle, and North Lark Storykeepers provisional until catalog aliases and reachability are proven.

#### Extended field 12 — Save and migration

Use the smallest existing save section. Capture the new fact, restore it, migrate older envelopes, tolerate an absent optional row, and make duplicate events idempotent. Define the pre-event, committed, refused, interrupted, and restored states. Do not encode prose branches in a panel cache. A rollback note must identify the event boundary and the owner responsible for undo or compensating projection.

#### Extended field 13 — Deterministic replay

Pin seed, event key, input order, and expected projection. Paired replays must agree on standing, access, route, roster, archive, or ending interpretation. Avoid wall-clock seeds, unordered iteration, hidden random choices, and locale-sensitive sorting. Include a late-arrival replay and a missing-record replay so optional content cannot alter the deterministic core unexpectedly.

#### Extended field 14 — UI and accessibility

The UI exposes a compact action label, expanded explanation, cost, consequence preview, focus order, keyboard and controller back behavior, readable long text, contrast, scaling, non-color cues, and confirmation for irreversible choices. Provide an audio or text alternative. If a record is missing, show a truthful unavailable state and preserve navigation. Archive and map panels consume projections; they do not own decisions.

#### Extended field 15 — Performance and lifecycle

Set budgets for catalog parse, query, event dispatch, archive projection, panel refresh, long text, and return visits. Load high-volume rows lazily, page them without changing order, dispose listeners on close, and avoid repeated full-catalog scans. Add one degradation path for a missing asset or provider. Note the smallest focused host smoke needed if the owner route is eventually implemented.

#### Extended field 16 — Acceptance and handoff

Acceptance requires premise evidence, owner and consumer proof, one reachable player command, save round trip, migration fixture, paired replay, accessibility review, performance notes, and a rollback boundary. The handoff names untouched shared paths and labels this as design scaffolding. The final image is practical: a repaired latch, an amended map, a divided bowl, a chalk mark, a quiet signal, or a door left open by consent.

### Wave 40 capsule 01: smoke-window arbitration at Cinderwillow Commons

**Opening and choice.** At **Cinderwillow Commons**, the player finds a practical problem that cannot be solved by rhetoric alone: a weather window is closing, a shared tool has two claimants, a missing person may be returning, a night signal is being misread, an apprentice is ready before the shelter is ready, a water ration has been counted twice, a quiet route carries an old debt, or a legacy object must be placed in another person’s hands. The player inspects the evidence, asks for consent, compares accounts, chooses a cost, defers, or leaves. The cost appears before commitment and a refusal keeps a safe return path.

**Authority and mechanic.** Route the action through the current owner for shelter culture and survivor vocations. Define one command, one event key, one resulting fact, one refusal result, one fallback, and one idempotency rule. A derived readiness view may combine existing standing, relationship, route, roster, shelter, archive, expedition, or ending facts, but it cannot become a second ledger or clock. The mechanic should make an ordinary task consequential: rescheduling a crossing changes who carries a tool, recording a signal changes which watch is asked to stand, or accepting a handover changes who is invited to the next meeting. The player can test the boundary in a low-risk version first.

**Place and shelter lore.** At **White River Classroom**, describe the builder, the repair that saved the room, the person who still pays for that repair, and the mark that remains unexplained. At **Indigo Ash Care Room**, place a contrasting trace: a patched hinge, a dry shelf, an erased route line, a bell rope, a teaching slate, or a bowl set aside. At **North Lark Meal Hall**, let a shelter custom make the history useful: a lamp is moved only after consent, a tool is returned sharpened, a guest cup is washed before dawn, or a route name is spoken once and then left unclaimed. Returning to the location shows a changed object before exposition.

**Characters and factions.** A resident speaks in concrete duties and notices who will carry the burden. A representative of **Cinderwillow Makers** uses public language and wants an auditable result. A voice from **White River Tutors** protects a custom that looks inefficient until its history is heard. **Indigo Ash Care Circle** values a scarce skill, while **North Lark Storykeepers** asks who will witness the consequence after the player leaves. Give each voice a promise, fear, boundary, apology, refusal, and callback. The late-game factional version may convene a coalition, certify a passage, steward a shelter custom, or preserve a memory, but it may request and witness only through existing authorities.

**Story and prose.** The scene opens with one quiet sentence about work: “The rope is dry enough for one more crossing,” “The cup was left where the missing person could find it,” or “The bell was rung before anyone agreed.” The player’s response changes who performs the task, what the journal remembers, and which later character feels entitled to speak. Add calm, pressure, failure, recovery, refusal, late-arrival, and missing-record variants. Use concrete objects, short silences, and a callback that makes the earlier mechanic visible without turning the packet into a lore lecture.

**Data and content volume.** Candidate rows carry schema_version, snake_case ID, owner, prerequisites, references, effects, fallback text, localization key, archive policy, retirement note, and missing-data behavior. Create arrival, inspection, task, hazard, rest, departure, return, calm, pressure, failure, recovery, refusal, and late-arrival variants. Keep the names of **Cinderwillow Makers**, **White River Tutors**, **Indigo Ash Care Circle**, and **North Lark Storykeepers** provisional until catalog aliases and reachability are proven. A missing optional row should collapse to a truthful unavailable state rather than alter the deterministic core.

**Persistence and replay.** Capture the smallest new fact through the existing save section. Define pre-action, committed, refused, interrupted, restored, migrated, and duplicate-event states. Pin the campaign seed, event key, input order, and expected projection. Paired replays must agree on standing, access, route, roster, archive, or ending interpretation, including the late-arrival and missing-record cases. Do not use wall-clock seeds, unordered iteration, locale-sensitive sorting, or hidden randomness in prose.

**UI, accessibility, and lifecycle.** Expose a compact action label, expanded explanation, cost, consequence preview, focus order, keyboard/controller close and back, readable long text, contrast, scaling, non-color cues, confirmation for irreversible actions, and text or audio alternatives. Panels consume owner projections and dispose listeners on close. High-volume rows load lazily and page without changing order. Set budgets for parse, query, dispatch, archive projection, refresh, and return visits; document the missing-provider path and the smallest eventual host smoke.

**Acceptance and handoff.** Accept the capsule only with premise evidence, owner and consumer proof, one reachable command, save round trip, migration fixture, paired replay, accessibility review, performance notes, and rollback. The handoff records untouched shared paths and labels the content as design scaffolding. The final image is small and physical: a cord retied, a cup passed over, a map corrected, a signal answered, a tool returned sharper, a meal divided, or a door left open because someone was asked first.

### Pass 439: The Amber Cinder Lesson

This pass extends shelter culture and survivor vocations with the amber cinder lesson. It is a proposal over the current authority owned by roster, relationship, skills, duty, needs, HobbySystem, SurvivorEducationSystem, ShelterArchiveSystem, and journal owners. The named factions and places are provisional labels, not catalog facts. Start with a source, data, consumer, and ownership audit; if an existing record already expresses the idea, fold this material into that record or stop. The player should make a legible choice that affects a practical task, a remembered relationship, a route, or a late-game interpretation.

#### 1. Premise evidence

Record the exact source path, API or JSON family, event producer, host route, and current plan entry that justify the amber cinder lesson. Name one absent seam and one collision to check. A proposal remains tagged unresolved until the premise is reproduced against current source.

#### 2. Owner contract

Route the command through roster, relationship, skills, duty, needs, HobbySystem, SurvivorEducationSystem, ShelterArchiveSystem, and journal owners. Define the input, output, refusal, fallback, and event key. Panels, maps, and prose consume the projection and never become a second ledger, graph, clock, route registry, roster, or ending resolver.

#### 3. Player action

Give the player inspect, ask, compare, repair, invite, ration, disclose, wait, or leave choices around the amber cinder lesson. Show cost before commitment, allow a respectful refusal, and provide recovery work or information after a failure unless the canonical owner defines a terminal outcome.

#### 4. State and save

Use the smallest existing save section. Capture and restore the new fact, migrate older envelopes, make duplicate events idempotent, and keep optional content safe when its record is absent. Do not add a local counter merely to make the prose conditional.

#### 5. Deterministic replay

Pin a seeded event key, input order, and expected result. A paired replay must produce the same standing, route, roster, archive, or ending projection. Avoid wall-clock seeds, unordered iteration, and hidden random choices in authored content.

#### 6. Location and shelter projection

Stage arrival, inspection, work, hazard, rest, departure, and return at East Yarrow Meal Hall. Add one physical trace, one shelter custom, one disputed memory, and one maintenance task so the location carries lore through action rather than exposition alone.

#### 7. Character and faction voice

Write distinct voices for a practical resident, an affected witness, and one representative of East Yarrow Storykeepers. Give each a promise, fear, boundary, refusal, apology, and late callback. Let a minor or absent voice receive a measurable consequence.

#### 8. Story and side-quest result

Build a side quest from an entry fact, one player action, one cost, one consequence, one refusal, one archive or journal fact, and a late-arrival variant. The scene may use prose, but the quest result must be an observable owner event that later content can read.

#### 9. UI and accessibility

Provide concise labels, expanded explanations, focus order, keyboard and controller back behavior, contrast, text scaling, non-color cues, irreversible-action confirmation, and a text or audio alternative. Long records must page or collapse without hiding the consequence.

#### 10. Performance and rollback

### Pass 449: The Recast Name

This pass extends shelter culture and survivor vocations with the recast name. It is a proposal over the current authority owned by roster, relationship, skills, duty, needs, HobbySystem, SurvivorEducationSystem, ShelterArchiveSystem, and journal owners. The named factions and places are provisional labels, not catalog facts. Start with a source, data, consumer, and ownership audit; if an existing record already expresses the idea, fold this material into that record or stop. The player should make a legible choice that affects a practical task, a remembered relationship, a route, or a late-game interpretation.

#### 1. Premise evidence

Record the exact source path, API or JSON family, event producer, host route, and current plan entry that justify the recast name. Name one absent seam and one collision to check. A proposal remains tagged unresolved until the premise is reproduced against current source.

#### 2. Owner contract

Route the command through roster, relationship, skills, duty, needs, HobbySystem, SurvivorEducationSystem, ShelterArchiveSystem, and journal owners. Define the input, output, refusal, fallback, and event key. Panels, maps, and prose consume the projection and never become a second ledger, graph, clock, route registry, roster, or ending resolver.

#### 3. Player action

Give the player inspect, ask, compare, repair, invite, ration, disclose, wait, or leave choices around the recast name. Show cost before commitment, allow a respectful refusal, and provide recovery work or information after a failure unless the canonical owner defines a terminal outcome.

#### 4. State and save

Use the smallest existing save section. Capture and restore the new fact, migrate older envelopes, make duplicate events idempotent, and keep optional content safe when its record is absent. Do not add a local counter merely to make the prose conditional.

#### 5. Deterministic replay

Pin a seeded event key, input order, and expected result. A paired replay must produce the same standing, route, roster, archive, or ending projection. Avoid wall-clock seeds, unordered iteration, and hidden random choices in authored content.

#### 6. Location and shelter projection

Stage arrival, inspection, work, hazard, rest, departure, and return at Mossglass Classroom. Add one physical trace, one shelter custom, one disputed memory, and one maintenance task so the location carries lore through action rather than exposition alone.

#### 7. Character and faction voice

Write distinct voices for a practical resident, an affected witness, and one representative of Mossglass Tutors. Give each a promise, fear, boundary, refusal, apology, and late callback. Let a minor or absent voice receive a measurable consequence.

#### 8. Story and side-quest result

Build a side quest from an entry fact, one player action, one cost, one consequence, one refusal, one archive or journal fact, and a late-arrival variant. The scene may use prose, but the quest result must be an observable owner event that later content can read.

#### 9. UI and accessibility

Provide concise labels, expanded explanations, focus order, keyboard and controller back behavior, contrast, text scaling, non-color cues, irreversible-action confirmation, and a text or audio alternative. Long records must page or collapse without hiding the consequence.

#### 10. Performance and rollback

Set budgets for catalog parse, query, event dispatch, panel refresh, archive projection, and long text. Include a missing-data path, a rollback boundary, a focused contract check, a save round trip, and a host smoke only where the owner route requires it.

## Wave 41 supplemental depth packets

These packets add volume to the current Wave 41 fields without introducing Fields 21–30. Each is a bounded design record for story, mechanics, systems, locations, shelter lore, character personalities, factions, late-game pressure, UI, persistence, replay, and performance.


### Supplemental packet 01: shelter culture and survivor vocations — Hollow Sun Classroom action 1

The scene opens at **Hollow Sun Classroom**, where the practical detail is more urgent than the ceremonial language: a damp ledger, a half-full water drum, a frayed coat, a relay key, a route marker, or an unlit lamp. A resident asks the player to inspect the public ledger. The player sees the cost before accepting and can refuse without losing the ability to return. The first response creates one canonical event and one journal or archive projection; later content reads that fact through the existing owner rather than through a panel cache.

**Mechanic and system contract.** Define the input, command, event key, result, refusal, fallback, and next choice. Use existing campaign, faction, relationship, roster, expedition, shelter, archive, or ending authority as appropriate. Stateful effects use the smallest current save section with capture, restore, migration, duplicate-event handling, and a seeded replay fixture. Do not create a second reputation score, route graph, relationship network, inventory ledger, calendar, or ending state. If the premise is absent in current source or data, keep this packet unresolved and record the exact missing seam.

**Location and shelter lore.** Explain who built Hollow Sun Classroom, what failed there, who repaired it, what custom grew from that repair, and who still pays its cost. Give the player one physical trace, one remembered phrase, one disputed interpretation, and one maintenance task. On a return visit, show the consequence before dialogue summarizes it. ## Wave 41 supplemental receipt

## Wave 41 extended depth layer

This larger tranche adds six extended packets per plan. They deepen the active twenty fields while keeping all mechanics, catalog rows, factions, locations, shelter customs, and late-game institutions provisional and owner-bound.

### Wave 41 extended depth packet 01: steady hearth compact at Frosted Alder Commons

#### Extended field 01 — Premise and canon

The steady hearth compact begins as a premise audit around Frosted Alder Commons. The player is asked to count the lamps before opening the door, but the proposal remains provisional until current source, JSON authority, event producer, host consumer, and ownership ledger are cited. Record the nearest existing seam, the exact absent seam, and the collision to exclude. If the premise is already represented, fold the prose into that owner and retire this packet rather than creating a duplicate.

#### Extended field 02 — Player loop

The loop has six readable beats: arrive at Frosted Alder Commons, inspect a practical sign, hear a resident’s account, choose a cost, perform one visible task, and return after the next weather or duty turn. The choice can preserve, delay, redirect, or refuse the request. Show the consequence before explanation. A failure gives information or a bounded recovery task unless the canonical owner defines a terminal result.

#### Extended field 03 — System contract

Route the command through the current owner for shelter culture and survivor vocations. Define command, event key, inputs, output fact, refusal, fallback, idempotency, and consumer. The packet may touch faction standing, route access, roster duty, shelter archive, relationship, expedition, or ending interpretation only through those authorities. It may not create a private truce score, route graph, calendar, inventory, reputation counter, or parallel legacy record.

#### Extended field 04 — Mechanic

Introduce one mechanic that makes maintenance and trust interact: a concession opens a safer task, a late repair changes a route window, or an honest admission reduces a future surprise. The mechanic should have a threshold, a visible cost, a reversible preparation state, and a deterministic result. The player can test the boundary in a low-risk scene before committing to the late-game version.

#### Extended field 05 — Location lore

At Hollow Sun Classroom, describe who built the room, which flood or fire altered it, who kept the key, and why one wall remains unpainted. Give the player a physical trace, a remembered phrase, a disputed interpretation, and a maintenance action. Returning to the site should show an object moved, repaired, withheld, or shared before any dialogue summarizes the change.

#### Extended field 06 — Shelter lore

The shelter projection keeps a custom tied to the same fact: a cup reserved for a messenger, a bell rung only after consent, a cord tied around a tool, or a bench left open for the missing. The custom has a practical function and a social cost. Its archive text must name the worker who sustains it and the person who objects without reducing either voice to exposition.

#### Extended field 07 — Character voices

Write three distinct voices. A resident of Hollow Sun Classroom notices labor and weather. A representative of Frosted Alder Makers speaks in careful public terms until the cost reaches a family or crew. A witness linked to Hollow Sun Tutors remembers a different sequence. Give each a promise, fear, boundary, apology, refusal, and late callback. Let a minor voice receive a measurable roster, route, archive, or ending consequence.

#### Extended field 08 — Faction politics

The faction layer distinguishes Frosted Alder Makers, Hollow Sun Tutors, Vermilion Soot Care Circle, and East Finch Storykeepers by resource, ritual, and risk rather than color. Frosted Alder Makers wants a reliable public record, Hollow Sun Tutors protects a route custom, Vermilion Soot Care Circle values a scarce repair skill, and East Finch Storykeepers demands a future witness. None is automatically virtuous. Coalition progress is a projection of existing standing and event facts, with dissent and abstention preserved.

#### Extended field 09 — Story and prose

The side quest opens with an ordinary sentence: someone asks whether the lamp, map, ledger, meal, or signal can wait one more night. The player’s answer changes who performs the task and what is remembered. Use restrained prose, concrete objects, and one silence that another character interprets differently. Add calm, pressure, failure, recovery, refusal, late-arrival, and missing-record variants.

#### Extended field 10 — Late-game system

The late-game form is a major faction or frontier institution that can only appear after several owner-bound facts agree. It may convene a coalition, certify a route, steward a shelter custom, or carry a legacy signal. Its powers are bounded: it can request, witness, schedule, or interpret. It cannot rewrite history, bypass save ownership, or silently convert provisional prose into canon.

#### Extended field 11 — Data and catalog

Candidate content rows for steady hearth compact carry schema_version, snake_case ID, owner, prerequisites, references, effects, fallback text, localization key, archive policy, retirement note, and missing-data behavior. Link every row to one canonical consumer and one command. Keep Vermilion Soot Care Room, East Finch Meal Hall, Vermilion Soot Care Circle, and East Finch Storykeepers provisional until catalog aliases and reachability are proven.

#### Extended field 12 — Save and migration

Use the smallest existing save section. Capture the new fact, restore it, migrate older envelopes, tolerate an absent optional row, and make duplicate events idempotent. Define the pre-event, committed, refused, interrupted, and restored states. Do not encode prose branches in a panel cache. A rollback note must identify the event boundary and the owner responsible for undo or compensating projection.

#### Extended field 13 — Deterministic replay

Pin seed, event key, input order, and expected projection. Paired replays must agree on standing, access, route, roster, archive, or ending interpretation. Avoid wall-clock seeds, unordered iteration, hidden random choices, and locale-sensitive sorting. Include a late-arrival replay and a missing-record replay so optional content cannot alter the deterministic core unexpectedly.

#### Extended field 14 — UI and accessibility

The UI exposes a compact action label, expanded explanation, cost, consequence preview, focus order, keyboard and controller back behavior, readable long text, contrast, scaling, non-color cues, and confirmation for irreversible choices. Provide an audio or text alternative. If a record is missing, show a truthful unavailable state and preserve navigation. Archive and map panels consume projections; they do not own decisions.

#### Extended field 15 — Performance and lifecycle

Set budgets for catalog parse, query, event dispatch, archive projection, panel refresh, long text, and return visits. Load high-volume rows lazily, page them without changing order, dispose listeners on close, and avoid repeated full-catalog scans. Add one degradation path for a missing asset or provider. Note the smallest focused host smoke needed if the owner route is eventually implemented.

#### Extended field 16 — Acceptance and handoff

Acceptance requires premise evidence, owner and consumer proof, one reachable player command, save round trip, migration fixture, paired replay, accessibility review, performance notes, and a rollback boundary. The handoff names untouched shared paths and labels this as design scaffolding. The final image is practical: a repaired latch, an amended map, a divided bowl, a chalk mark, a quiet signal, or a door left open by consent.

### Wave 41 capsule 01: frost-window arbitration at Frosted Alder Commons

**Opening and choice.** At **Frosted Alder Commons**, the player finds a practical problem that cannot be solved by rhetoric alone: a weather window is closing, a shared tool has two claimants, a missing person may be returning, a night signal is being misread, an apprentice is ready before the shelter is ready, a water ration has been counted twice, a quiet route carries an old debt, or a legacy object must be placed in another person’s hands. The player inspects the evidence, asks for consent, compares accounts, chooses a cost, defers, or leaves. The cost appears before commitment and a refusal keeps a safe return path.

**Authority and mechanic.** Route the action through the current owner for shelter culture and survivor vocations. Define one command, one event key, one resulting fact, one refusal result, one fallback, and one idempotency rule. A derived readiness view may combine existing standing, relationship, route, roster, shelter, archive, expedition, or ending facts, but it cannot become a second ledger or clock. The mechanic should make an ordinary task consequential: rescheduling a crossing changes who carries a tool, recording a signal changes which watch is asked to stand, or accepting a handover changes who is invited to the next meeting. The player can test the boundary in a low-risk version first.

**Place and shelter lore.** At **Hollow Sun Classroom**, describe the builder, the repair that saved the room, the person who still pays for that repair, and the mark that remains unexplained. At **Vermilion Soot Care Room**, place a contrasting trace: a patched hinge, a dry shelf, an erased route line, a bell rope, a teaching slate, or a bowl set aside. At **East Finch Meal Hall**, let a shelter custom make the history useful: a lamp is moved only after consent, a tool is returned sharpened, a guest cup is washed before dawn, or a route name is spoken once and then left unclaimed. Returning to the location shows a changed object before exposition.

**Characters and factions.** A resident speaks in concrete duties and notices who will carry the burden. A representative of **Frosted Alder Makers** uses public language and wants an auditable result. A voice from **Hollow Sun Tutors** protects a custom that looks inefficient until its history is heard. **Vermilion Soot Care Circle** values a scarce skill, while **East Finch Storykeepers** asks who will witness the consequence after the player leaves. Give each voice a promise, fear, boundary, apology, refusal, and callback. The late-game factional version may convene a coalition, certify a passage, steward a shelter custom, or preserve a memory, but it may request and witness only through existing authorities.

**Story and prose.** The scene opens with one quiet sentence about work: “The rope is dry enough for one more crossing,” “The cup was left where the missing person could find it,” or “The bell was rung before anyone agreed.” The player’s response changes who performs the task, what the journal remembers, and which later character feels entitled to speak. Add calm, pressure, failure, recovery, refusal, late-arrival, and missing-record variants. Use concrete objects, short silences, and a callback that makes the earlier mechanic visible without turning the packet into a lore lecture.

**Data and content volume.** Candidate rows carry schema_version, snake_case ID, owner, prerequisites, references, effects, fallback text, localization key, archive policy, retirement note, and missing-data behavior. Create arrival, inspection, task, hazard, rest, departure, return, calm, pressure, failure, recovery, refusal, and late-arrival variants. Keep the names of **Frosted Alder Makers**, **Hollow Sun Tutors**, **Vermilion Soot Care Circle**, and **East Finch Storykeepers** provisional until catalog aliases and reachability are proven. A missing optional row should collapse to a truthful unavailable state rather than alter the deterministic core.

**Persistence and replay.** Capture the smallest new fact through the existing save section. Define pre-action, committed, refused, interrupted, restored, migrated, and duplicate-event states. Pin the campaign seed, event key, input order, and expected projection. Paired replays must agree on standing, access, route, roster, archive, or ending interpretation, including the late-arrival and missing-record cases. Do not use wall-clock seeds, unordered iteration, locale-sensitive sorting, or hidden randomness in prose.

**UI, accessibility, and lifecycle.** Expose a compact action label, expanded explanation, cost, consequence preview, focus order, keyboard/controller close and back, readable long text, contrast, scaling, non-color cues, confirmation for irreversible actions, and text or audio alternatives. Panels consume owner projections and dispose listeners on close. High-volume rows load lazily and page without changing order. Set budgets for parse, query, dispatch, archive projection, refresh, and return visits; document the missing-provider path and the smallest eventual host smoke.

**Acceptance and handoff.** Accept the capsule only with premise evidence, owner and consumer proof, one reachable command, save round trip, migration fixture, paired replay, accessibility review, performance notes, and rollback. The handoff records untouched shared paths and labels the content as design scaffolding. The final image is small and physical: a cord retied, a cup passed over, a map corrected, a signal answered, a tool returned sharper, a meal divided, or a door left open because someone was asked first.

## Wave 42 supplemental depth packets

These packets add volume to the current Wave 42 fields without introducing Fields 21–30. Each is a bounded design record for story, mechanics, systems, locations, shelter lore, character personalities, factions, late-game pressure, UI, persistence, replay, and performance.


### Supplemental packet 01: shelter culture and survivor vocations — Rustwater Classroom action 1

The scene opens at **Rustwater Classroom**, where the practical detail is more urgent than the ceremonial language: a damp ledger, a half-full water drum, a frayed coat, a relay key, a route marker, or an unlit lamp. A resident asks the player to inspect the public ledger. The player sees the cost before accepting and can refuse without losing the ability to return. The first response creates one canonical event and one journal or archive projection; later content reads that fact through the existing owner rather than through a panel cache.

**Mechanic and system contract.** Define the input, command, event key, result, refusal, fallback, and next choice. Use existing campaign, faction, relationship, roster, expedition, shelter, archive, or ending authority as appropriate. Stateful effects use the smallest current save section with capture, restore, migration, duplicate-event handling, and a seeded replay fixture. Do not create a second reputation score, route graph, relationship network, inventory ledger, calendar, or ending state. If the premise is absent in current source or data, keep this packet unresolved and record the exact missing seam.

**Location and shelter lore.** Explain who built Rustwater Classroom, what failed there, who repaired it, what custom grew from that repair, and who still pays its cost. Give the player one physical trace, one remembered phrase, one disputed interpretation, and one maintenance task. On a return visit, show the consequence before dialogue summarizes it. A quiet shelter detail should carry history: a bed rotated away from a draft, a cup reserved for visitors, a chalk line refreshed after rain, or a tool returned sharper than it was found.

**Character and faction direction.** The resident speaks plainly and notices labor before symbolism. A witness from **Rustwater Tutors** uses formal language until a shortage makes the stakes concrete. A third voice may be an apprentice, courier, absent person represented by an object, or elder who remembers a different version. Give each a promise, fear, boundary, apology, refusal, and late callback. Let a minor voice receive one measurable outcome in the roster, route, archive, relationship, or ending projection.

**Story, UI, and verification.** The side quest needs an entry condition, player action, cost, consequence, refusal branch, archive fact, late-arrival variant, and missing-record variant. Prose should reveal the mechanic through ordinary work. The UI needs a compact label, expanded explanation, focus order, keyboard/controller close and back, readable long text, contrast, non-color cues, and confirmation for irreversible actions. Acceptance requires premise evidence, owner and consumer proof, focused contract or data checks, save round trip, paired deterministic replay, performance notes, and a rollback boundary. The packet is not an implementation claim; it is ready only for a safe-slice review.

### Wave 42 extended depth packet 01: open table compact at Blue Thistle Commons

#### Extended field 01 — Premise and canon

The open table compact begins as a premise audit around Blue Thistle Commons. The player is asked to count the lamps before opening the door, but the proposal remains provisional until current source, JSON authority, event producer, host consumer, and ownership ledger are cited. Record the nearest existing seam, the exact absent seam, and the collision to exclude. If the premise is already represented, fold the prose into that owner and retire this packet rather than creating a duplicate.

#### Extended field 02 — Player loop

The loop has six readable beats: arrive at Blue Thistle Commons, inspect a practical sign, hear a resident’s account, choose a cost, perform one visible task, and return after the next weather or duty turn. The choice can preserve, delay, redirect, or refuse the request. Show the consequence before explanation. A failure gives information or a bounded recovery task unless the canonical owner defines a terminal result.

#### Extended field 03 — System contract

Route the command through the current owner for shelter culture and survivor vocations. Define command, event key, inputs, output fact, refusal, fallback, idempotency, and consumer. The packet may touch faction standing, route access, roster duty, shelter archive, relationship, expedition, or ending interpretation only through those authorities. It may not create a private truce score, route graph, calendar, inventory, reputation counter, or parallel legacy record.

#### Extended field 04 — Mechanic

Introduce one mechanic that makes maintenance and trust interact: a concession opens a safer task, a late repair changes a route window, or an honest admission reduces a future surprise. The mechanic should have a threshold, a visible cost, a reversible preparation state, and a deterministic result. The player can test the boundary in a low-risk scene before committing to the late-game version.

#### Extended field 05 — Location lore

At Rustwater Classroom, describe who built the room, which flood or fire altered it, who kept the key, and why one wall remains unpainted. Give the player a physical trace, a remembered phrase, a disputed interpretation, and a maintenance action. Returning to the site should show an object moved, repaired, withheld, or shared before any dialogue summarizes the change.

#### Extended field 06 — Shelter lore

The shelter projection keeps a custom tied to the same fact: a cup reserved for a messenger, a bell rung only after consent, a cord tied around a tool, or a bench left open for the missing. The custom has a practical function and a social cost. Its archive text must name the worker who sustains it and the person who objects without reducing either voice to exposition.

#### Extended field 07 — Character voices

Write three distinct voices. A resident of Rustwater Classroom notices labor and weather. A representative of Blue Thistle Makers speaks in careful public terms until the cost reaches a family or crew. A witness linked to Rustwater Tutors remembers a different sequence. Give each a promise, fear, boundary, apology, refusal, and late callback. Let a minor voice receive a measurable roster, route, archive, or ending consequence.

#### Extended field 08 — Faction politics

The faction layer distinguishes Blue Thistle Makers, Rustwater Tutors, Golden Cinder Care Circle, and West Heron Storykeepers by resource, ritual, and risk rather than color. Blue Thistle Makers wants a reliable public record, Rustwater Tutors protects a route custom, Golden Cinder Care Circle values a scarce repair skill, and West Heron Storykeepers demands a future witness. None is automatically virtuous. Coalition progress is a projection of existing standing and event facts, with dissent and abstention preserved.

#### Extended field 09 — Story and prose

The side quest opens with an ordinary sentence: someone asks whether the lamp, map, ledger, meal, or signal can wait one more night. The player’s answer changes who performs the task and what is remembered. Use restrained prose, concrete objects, and one silence that another character interprets differently. Add calm, pressure, failure, recovery, refusal, late-arrival, and missing-record variants.

#### Extended field 10 — Late-game system

The late-game form is a major faction or frontier institution that can only appear after several owner-bound facts agree. It may convene a coalition, certify a route, steward a shelter custom, or carry a legacy signal. Its powers are bounded: it can request, witness, schedule, or interpret. It cannot rewrite history, bypass save ownership, or silently convert provisional prose into canon.

#### Extended field 11 — Data and catalog

Candidate content rows for open table compact carry schema_version, snake_case ID, owner, prerequisites, references, effects, fallback text, localization key, archive policy, retirement note, and missing-data behavior. Link every row to one canonical consumer and one command. Keep Golden Cinder Care Room, West Heron Meal Hall, Golden Cinder Care Circle, and West Heron Storykeepers provisional until catalog aliases and reachability are proven.

#### Extended field 12 — Save and migration

Use the smallest existing save section. Capture the new fact, restore it, migrate older envelopes, tolerate an absent optional row, and make duplicate events idempotent. Define the pre-event, committed, refused, interrupted, and restored states. Do not encode prose branches in a panel cache. A rollback note must identify the event boundary and the owner responsible for undo or compensating projection.

#### Extended field 13 — Deterministic replay

Pin seed, event key, input order, and expected projection. Paired replays must agree on standing, access, route, roster, archive, or ending interpretation. Avoid wall-clock seeds, unordered iteration, hidden random choices, and locale-sensitive sorting. Include a late-arrival replay and a missing-record replay so optional content cannot alter the deterministic core unexpectedly.

#### Extended field 14 — UI and accessibility

The UI exposes a compact action label, expanded explanation, cost, consequence preview, focus order, keyboard and controller back behavior, readable long text, contrast, scaling, non-color cues, and confirmation for irreversible choices. Provide an audio or text alternative. If a record is missing, show a truthful unavailable state and preserve navigation. Archive and map panels consume projections; they do not own decisions.

#### Extended field 15 — Performance and lifecycle

Set budgets for catalog parse, query, event dispatch, archive projection, panel refresh, long text, and return visits. Load high-volume rows lazily, page them without changing order, dispose listeners on close, and avoid repeated full-catalog scans. Add one degradation path for a missing asset or provider. Note the smallest focused host smoke needed if the owner route is eventually implemented.

#### Extended field 16 — Acceptance and handoff

Acceptance requires premise evidence, owner and consumer proof, one reachable player command, save round trip, migration fixture, paired replay, accessibility review, performance notes, and a rollback boundary. The handoff names untouched shared paths and labels this as design scaffolding. The final image is practical: a repaired latch, an amended map, a divided bowl, a chalk mark, a quiet signal, or a door left open by consent.

### Wave 42 capsule 01: blue-hour arbitration at Blue Thistle Commons

**Opening and choice.** At **Blue Thistle Commons**, the player finds a practical problem that cannot be solved by rhetoric alone: a weather window is closing, a shared tool has two claimants, a missing person may be returning, a night signal is being misread, an apprentice is ready before the shelter is ready, a water ration has been counted twice, a quiet route carries an old debt, or a legacy object must be placed in another person’s hands. The player inspects the evidence, asks for consent, compares accounts, chooses a cost, defers, or leaves. The cost appears before commitment and a refusal keeps a safe return path.

**Authority and mechanic.** Route the action through the current owner for shelter culture and survivor vocations. Define one command, one event key, one resulting fact, one refusal result, one fallback, and one idempotency rule. A derived readiness view may combine existing standing, relationship, route, roster, shelter, archive, expedition, or ending facts, but it cannot become a second ledger or clock. The mechanic should make an ordinary task consequential: rescheduling a crossing changes who carries a tool, recording a signal changes which watch is asked to stand, or accepting a handover changes who is invited to the next meeting. The player can test the boundary in a low-risk version first.

**Place and shelter lore.** At **Rustwater Classroom**, describe the builder, the repair that saved the room, the person who still pays for that repair, and the mark that remains unexplained. At **Golden Cinder Care Room**, place a contrasting trace: a patched hinge, a dry shelf, an erased route line, a bell rope, a teaching slate, or a bowl set aside. At **West Heron Meal Hall**, let a shelter custom make the history useful: a lamp is moved only after consent, a tool is returned sharpened, a guest cup is washed before dawn, or a route name is spoken once and then left unclaimed. Returning to the location shows a changed object before exposition.

**Characters and factions.** A resident speaks in concrete duties and notices who will carry the burden. A representative of **Blue Thistle Makers** uses public language and wants an auditable result. A voice from **Rustwater Tutors** protects a custom that looks inefficient until its history is heard. **Golden Cinder Care Circle** values a scarce skill, while **West Heron Storykeepers** asks who will witness the consequence after the player leaves. Give each voice a promise, fear, boundary, apology, refusal, and callback. The late-game factional version may convene a coalition, certify a passage, steward a shelter custom, or preserve a memory, but it may request and witness only through existing authorities.

**Story and prose.** The scene opens with one quiet sentence about work: “The rope is dry enough for one more crossing,” “The cup was left where the missing person could find it,” or “The bell was rung before anyone agreed.” The player’s response changes who performs the task, what the journal remembers, and which later character feels entitled to speak. Add calm, pressure, failure, recovery, refusal, late-arrival, and missing-record variants. Use concrete objects, short silences, and a callback that makes the earlier mechanic visible without turning the packet into a lore lecture.

**Data and content volume.** Candidate rows carry schema_version, snake_case ID, owner, prerequisites, references, effects, fallback text, localization key, archive policy, retirement note, and missing-data behavior. Create arrival, inspection, task, hazard, rest, departure, return, calm, pressure, failure, recovery, refusal, and late-arrival variants. Keep the names of **Blue Thistle Makers**, **Rustwater Tutors**, **Golden Cinder Care Circle**, and **West Heron Storykeepers** provisional until catalog aliases and reachability are proven. A missing optional row should collapse to a truthful unavailable state rather than alter the deterministic core.

**Persistence and replay.** Capture the smallest new fact through the existing save section. Define pre-action, committed, refused, interrupted, restored, migrated, and duplicate-event states. Pin the campaign seed, event key, input order, and expected projection. Paired replays must agree on standing, access, route, roster, archive, or ending interpretation, including the late-arrival and missing-record cases. Do not use wall-clock seeds, unordered iteration, locale-sensitive sorting, or hidden randomness in prose.

**UI, accessibility, and lifecycle.** Expose a compact action label, expanded explanation, cost, consequence preview, focus order, keyboard/controller close and back, readable long text, contrast, scaling, non-color cues, confirmation for irreversible actions, and text or audio alternatives. Panels consume owner projections and dispose listeners on close. High-volume rows load lazily and page without changing order. Set budgets for parse, query, dispatch, archive projection, refresh, and return visits; document the missing-provider path and the smallest eventual host smoke.

**Acceptance and handoff.** Accept the capsule only with premise evidence, owner and consumer proof, one reachable command, save round trip, migration fixture, paired replay, accessibility review, performance notes, and rollback. The handoff records untouched shared paths and labels the content as design scaffolding. The final image is small and physical: a cord retied, a cup passed over, a map corrected, a signal answered, a tool returned sharper, a meal divided, or a door left open because someone was asked first.

It may not create a private truce score, route graph, calendar, inventory, reputation counter, or parallel legacy record.

#### Extended field 04 — Mechanic

Introduce one mechanic that makes maintenance and trust interact: a concession opens a safer task, a late repair changes a route window, or an honest admission reduces a future surprise. The mechanic should have a threshold, a visible cost, a reversible preparation state, and a deterministic result. The player can test the boundary in a low-risk scene before committing to the late-game version.

#### Extended field 05 — Location lore

At Ashwater Classroom, describe who built the room, which flood or fire altered it, who kept the key, and why one wall remains unpainted. Give the player a physical trace, a remembered phrase, a disputed interpretation, and a maintenance action. Returning to the site should show an object moved, repaired, withheld, or shared before any dialogue summarizes the change.

#### Extended field 06 — Shelter lore

The shelter projection keeps a custom tied to the same fact: a cup reserved for a messenger, a bell rung only after consent, a cord tied around a tool, or a bench left open for the missing. The custom has a practical function and a social cost. Its archive text must name the worker who sustains it and the person who objects without reducing either voice to exposition.

#### Extended field 07 — Character voices

Write three distinct voices. A resident of Ashwater Classroom notices labor and weather. A representative of Quiet Juniper Makers speaks in careful public terms until the cost reaches a family or crew. A witness linked to Ashwater Tutors remembers a different sequence. Give each a promise, fear, boundary, apology, refusal, and late callback. Let a minor voice receive a measurable roster, route, archive, or ending consequence.

#### Extended field 08 — Faction politics

The faction layer distinguishes Quiet Juniper Makers, Ashwater Tutors, Bronze Haze Care Circle, and South Wren Storykeepers by resource, ritual, and risk rather than color. Quiet Juniper Makers wants a reliable public record, Ashwater Tutors protects a route custom, Bronze Haze Care Circle values a scarce repair skill, and South Wren Storykeepers demands a future witness. None is automatically virtuous. Coalition progress is a projection of existing standing and event facts, with dissent and abstention preserved.

#### Extended field 09 — Story and prose

The side quest opens with an ordinary sentence: someone asks whether the lamp, map, ledger, meal, or signal can wait one more night. The player’s answer changes who performs the task and what is remembered. Use restrained prose, concrete objects, and one silence that another character interprets differently. Add calm, pressure, failure, recovery, refusal, late-arrival, and missing-record variants.

#### Extended field 10 — Late-game system

The late-game form is a major faction or frontier institution that can only appear after several owner-bound facts agree. It may convene a coalition, certify a route, steward a shelter custom, or carry a legacy signal. Its powers are bounded: it can request, witness, schedule, or interpret. It cannot rewrite history, bypass save ownership, or silently convert provisional prose into canon.

#### Extended field 11 — Data and catalog

Candidate content rows for listening table compact carry schema_version, snake_case ID, owner, prerequisites, references, effects, fallback text, localization key, archive policy, retirement note, and missing-data behavior. Link every row to one canonical consumer and one command. Keep Bronze Haze Care Room, South Wren Meal Hall, Bronze Haze Care Circle, and South Wren Storykeepers provisional until catalog aliases and reachability are proven.

#### Extended field 12 — Save and migration

Use the smallest existing save section. Capture the new fact, restore it, migrate older envelopes, tolerate an absent optional row, and make duplicate events idempotent. Define the pre-event, committed, refused, interrupted, and restored states. Do not encode prose branches in a panel cache. A rollback note must identify the event boundary and the owner responsible for undo or compensating projection.

#### Extended field 13 — Deterministic replay

Pin seed, event key, input order, and expected projection. Paired replays must agree on standing, access, route, roster, archive, or ending interpretation. Avoid wall-clock seeds, unordered iteration, hidden random choices, and locale-sensitive sorting. Include a late-arrival replay and a missing-record replay so optional content cannot alter the deterministic core unexpectedly.

#### Extended field 14 — UI and accessibility

The UI exposes a compact action label, expanded explanation, cost, consequence preview, focus order, keyboard and controller back behavior, readable long text, contrast, scaling, non-color cues, and confirmation for irreversible choices. Provide an audio or text alternative. If a record is missing, show a truthful unavailable state and preserve navigation. Archive and map panels consume projections; they do not own decisions.

#### Extended field 15 — Performance and lifecycle

Set budgets for catalog parse, query, event dispatch, archive projection, panel refresh, long text, and return visits. Load high-volume rows lazily, page them without changing order, dispose listeners on close, and avoid repeated full-catalog scans. Add one degradation path for a missing asset or provider. Note the smallest focused host smoke needed if the owner route is eventually implemented.

#### Extended field 16 — Acceptance and handoff

Acceptance requires premise evidence, owner and consumer proof, one reachable player command, save round trip, migration fixture, paired replay, accessibility review, performance notes, and a rollback boundary. The handoff names untouched shared paths and labels this as design scaffolding. The final image is practical: a repaired latch, an amended map, a divided bowl, a chalk mark, a quiet signal, or a door left open by consent.
